text: The relationship api.example --[references]--> api.schema is only an inferred link, because in OpenAPI 3.0 an Example Object never points to a Schema and is merely co-located with one, so 'references' is the wrong predicate.
proposed_change: Remove the references relationship from api.example to api.schema, or replace it with a path via the elements that actually hold both.

subject: api.example
text: The relationship api.example --[associated-with]--> api.operation is indirect, because an Example attaches to an operation only through a parameter, header or media type.
proposed_change: Remove the direct associated-with relationship to api.operation and rely on the path through parameter, header or media type.

subject: api.example
text: A path via parameter, header or media type may make both the api.example references-schema and associated-with-operation relationships redundant.
proposed_change: Drop both relationships if the indirect paths through parameter, header and media type already express the connection.

subject: api.externaldocumentation
text: The associated-with relationship from api.externaldocumentation to api.info is questionable and redundant, because OpenAPI does not allow externalDocs to attach to Info; it attaches to the root document, which already has a serves relationship.
proposed_change: Remove the associated-with relationship from api.externaldocumentation to api.info.

subject: api.externaldocumentation
text: api.externaldocumentation has no relationship to api.tag even though Tag is a valid attachment point for externalDocs.
proposed_change: Add a serves relationship from api.externaldocumentation to api.tag.

subject: api.header
text: The associated-with relationship from api.header to api.securityscheme is weak because the OpenAPI document has no structural link between them, only an apiKey scheme naming the same header string, so it should be derived or inferred rather than declared.
proposed_change: Make the header-to-securityscheme association a derived or inferred relationship instead of a declared one.

subject: api.header
text: The specializes relationship from api.header to api.parameter is only conceptual at the specification level and does not connect two instance-level elements.
proposed_change: Remove the specializes relationship between api.header and api.parameter or replace it with a relationship that holds between instances.

subject: api.info
text: The relationship api.info --[associated-with]--> api.openapidocument is weak and redundant, because Info cannot exist without its document and the inverse api.openapidocument composes api.info already expresses the accurate structural relation.
proposed_change: Remove the api.info associated-with api.openapidocument relationship and keep api.openapidocument composes api.info.

subject: api.info
text: The relationships api.info aggregates api.contact and api.info aggregates api.license may be better expressed as composes, since Contact and License are nested and document-bound, unless shared contacts or licenses are intended.
proposed_change: Change the predicate of both relationships from aggregates to composes, unless shared contacts or licenses are intended.

subject: api.license
text: The relationship api.license --associated-with--> api.openapidocument is redundant if the Info-to-document composition is already modeled, since License reaches the document transitively through Info.
proposed_change: Remove the direct associated-with relationship from api.license to api.openapidocument.

subject: api.license
text: The api.info --aggregates--> api.license relationship understates the structural nesting of License inside Info; the containment should be modeled as composition (License nested in Info, composed into OpenAPIDocument) rather than aggregation or loose association.
proposed_change: Change the Info-to-License relationship to composes, or express License containment via Info, instead of a direct association to the document.

subject: api.link
text: The relationship api.link references api.schema has no corresponding field in the OpenAPI Link Object; it exists only indirectly via runtime expressions.
proposed_change: Remove the api.link references api.schema relationship.

subject: api.link
text: The relationship api.link references api.tag has no corresponding field in the OpenAPI Link Object and is only indirect via the target operation's tags; it is derivable from link→operation plus operation→tag.
proposed_change: Remove the api.link references api.tag relationship, since it is derivable from link→operation and operation→tag.

subject: api.link
text: The relationship api.link uses api.server is valid because the OpenAPI Link Object has a 'server' field.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: api.mediatype
text: api.mediatype has both aggregates and composes relationships to api.encoding, which are contradictory because Encoding cannot exist outside its MediaType, so only composes should remain.
proposed_change: Remove the api.mediatype aggregates api.encoding relationship and keep composes.

subject: api.mediatype
text: The associated-with relationship from api.mediatype to api.header is indirect (it goes via Encoding) and therefore redundant.
proposed_change: Remove the api.mediatype associated-with api.header relationship.

subject: api.mediatype
text: The serves relationships from api.mediatype to api.requestbody and api.response misstate the structure, because RequestBody and Response compose MediaType through their content map.
proposed_change: Replace the serves relationships with the inverse composed-of relationships from api.mediatype to api.requestbody and api.response.

subject: api.oauthflow
text: The relationship api.oauthflow aggregates api.tag is dubious because OAuthFlow has no structural link to tags, only an indirect one via scopes on operations.
proposed_change: Remove the aggregates relationship from api.oauthflow to api.tag.

subject: api.oauthflow
text: The relationship api.oauthflow associated-with api.oauthflows understates a real composition, because the OAuthFlows container owns the flow.
proposed_change: Replace the associated-with relationship with composition (the container composes the flow), or drop it in favor of api.oauthflows composes api.oauthflow.

subject: api.oauthflow
text: The relationship api.oauthflow serves api.securityscheme is really composition via OAuthFlows, not a service relationship.
proposed_change: Replace the serves relationship with a composition-based relationship via OAuthFlows, or remove it.

subject: api.oauthflow
text: The relationship api.oauthflow associated-with api.ratelimit has no basis in the spec beyond gateway conventions.
proposed_change: Remove the associated-with relationship from api.oauthflow to api.ratelimit.

subject: api.oauthflows
text: api.oauthflows has both aggregates and composes relationships to api.oauthflow, which are contradictory because OAuthFlow cannot exist outside OAuthFlows, so composes is correct.
proposed_change: Remove the aggregates relationship from api.oauthflows to api.oauthflow and keep composes.

subject: api.oauthflows
text: The serves relationship from api.oauthflows to api.securityscheme should be composition, since the security scheme composes OAuthFlows (and api.securityscheme already composes api.oauthflows).
proposed_change: Replace the serves relationship to api.securityscheme with composition (or remove it in favor of securityscheme composes oauthflows).

subject: api.oauthflows
text: The associated-with relationships from api.oauthflows to api.components and api.operation are indirect, running through SecurityScheme, and duplicate those paths.
proposed_change: Remove the associated-with relationships to api.components and api.operation.

subject: api.openapidocument
text: The composes relationship from api.openapidocument to api.responses is wrong because a Responses map is scoped to an operation, not the document.
proposed_change: Remove the relationship and have api.operation compose api.responses instead.

subject: api.openapidocument
text: The composes relationship from api.openapidocument to api.schema duplicates the path through api.components, which already holds schemas.
proposed_change: Remove the direct composes relationship to api.schema and keep the path via api.components.

subject: api.openapidocument
text: The depends-on relationship from api.openapidocument to technology.technologyservice belongs to the implementing component, not the document.
proposed_change: Remove it from api.openapidocument and express the technology dependency on the implementing application component.

subject: api.openapidocument
text: The realizes relationship from api.openapidocument to business.businessservice skips the application layer.
proposed_change: Remove the direct realizes link to business.businessservice and route it through the application layer.

subject: api.openapidocument
text: The serves relationship from api.openapidocument to motivation.stakeholder is weak.
proposed_change: Remove the serves relationship to motivation.stakeholder.

subject: api.operation
text: The relationship api.operation composes api.paths is inverted, because Paths contains PathItems which contain operations.
proposed_change: Remove or reverse it so that api.paths (via api.pathitem) composes api.operation.

subject: api.operation
text: The relationships api.operation composes api.schema and api.operation references api.schema overlap, differing only in inline versus $ref.
proposed_change: Consolidate into a single relationship between api.operation and api.schema.

subject: api.operation
text: The relationships api.operation aggregates api.tag and api.operation references api.tag overlap, differing only in inline versus $ref.
proposed_change: Consolidate into a single relationship between api.operation and api.tag.

subject: api.operation
text: The relationship api.operation delivers api.response duplicates api.operation composes api.responses.
proposed_change: Remove one of the two relationships.

subject: api.operation
text: The relationships api.operation realizes motivation.goal and realizes motivation.outcome use the wrong predicate; they should be supports or delivers.
proposed_change: Change the predicate from realizes to supports or delivers.

subject: api.operation
text: The relationships api.operation realizes business.businessprocess and api.operation triggers business.businessprocess overlap.
proposed_change: Consolidate them or define a boundary between realizes and triggers for business processes.

subject: api.parameter
text: The relationship api.parameter references api.operation is inverted, since operations contain parameters; an operation-to-parameter composes/aggregates relationship fits better (api.operation aggregates api.parameter already exists).
proposed_change: Replace the parameter→operation references relationship with operation composes/aggregates parameter.

subject: api.parameter
text: The relationship api.parameter references api.tag has no basis in OpenAPI 3.0 because Parameter Objects have no tags field.
proposed_change: Remove the api.parameter references api.tag relationship.

subject: api.parameter
text: The relationship api.parameter references api.schema would be more precise with a constrained-by predicate than references.
proposed_change: Change the predicate of parameter→schema from references to constrained-by.

subject: api.pathitem
text: The relationship api.pathitem references api.externaldocumentation is questionable because OpenAPI's Path Item Object has no externalDocs field, so it is only realizable via description links.
proposed_change: Remove the references relationship from api.pathitem to api.externaldocumentation.

subject: api.pathitem
text: The relationship api.pathitem realizes business.businessfunction is unusual because business behaviour is normally realized by the operation or an application service rather than directly by a path item.
proposed_change: Remove the realizes relationship from api.pathitem to business.businessfunction and rely on operation-level or application-service realization.

subject: api.pathitem
text: The relationship api.pathitem serves application.applicationcomponent is more naturally expressed at the operation level than at the path item level.
proposed_change: Move the serves relationship to application.applicationcomponent from api.pathitem to api.operation.

subject: api.paths
text: api.paths has both an aggregates and a composes relationship to api.pathitem, which express the same meaning redundantly; composes should be kept and aggregates reserved for $ref'd components/pathItems.
proposed_change: Remove the aggregates relationship from api.paths to api.pathitem (or restrict it to $ref'd components/pathItems) and keep composes.

subject: api.ratelimit
text: The relationships api.ratelimit governs api.operation and api.ratelimit serves api.operation are redundant because both attach a rate limit to an operation, and 'governs' fits better.
proposed_change: Merge the serves relationship to api.operation into the governs (or constrains) relationship.

subject: api.ratelimit
text: The 'serves' predicate from api.ratelimit to api.operation and api.pathitem inverts the usual meaning, since a rate limit restricts rather than provides functionality.
proposed_change: Replace the serves relationships with governs/constrains semantics toward api.operation and api.pathitem.

subject: api.requestbody
text: The relationships api.requestbody aggregates api.mediatype and api.requestbody composes api.mediatype are redundant and conflicting; composes is the correct one since media types live only inside the content map.
proposed_change: Remove the aggregates relationship from api.requestbody to api.mediatype and keep composes.

subject: api.requestbody
text: The relationships from api.requestbody to api.example (aggregates), api.encoding (associated-with) and api.schema (references) are indirect because these elements hang off api.mediatype, not api.requestbody.
proposed_change: Remove the direct relationships from api.requestbody to api.example, api.encoding and api.schema, leaving them on api.mediatype.

subject: api.requestbody
text: The relationship api.requestbody serves api.operation has odd semantics and points the wrong way; the operation should own the request body as part of its contract.
proposed_change: Remove requestbody serves operation and express the link as api.operation composes (or aggregates) api.requestbody.

subject: api.response
text: api.response has both aggregates and composes relationships to api.header, which express overlapping meaning; they should be distinguished (e.g. $ref-reused versus inline) or one dropped.
proposed_change: Define aggregates as $ref-reused headers and composes as inline headers, or drop one of the two.

subject: api.response
text: api.response has both aggregates and composes relationships to api.mediatype, which express overlapping meaning; they should be distinguished (e.g. $ref-reused versus inline) or one dropped.
proposed_change: Define aggregates as $ref-reused media types and composes as inline media types, or drop one of the two.

subject: api.response
text: The aggregates and references relationships from api.response to api.schema overlap in meaning.
proposed_change: Drop one of the two or define a clear distinction between them.

subject: api.response
text: The direct api.response to api.schema (aggregates and references) and api.response references api.example relationships are indirect in OAS 3.0, since responses reach schemas and examples only through media types or headers, making them transitive shortcuts of the mediatype/header relationships.
proposed_change: Remove the direct response-to-schema and response-to-example relationships, leaving the paths via api.mediatype and api.header.

subject: api.responses
text: The relationships api.responses aggregates api.header, api.responses aggregates api.schema and api.responses references api.link are transitive shortcuts, because headers, schemas and links belong to individual Response objects (or MediaType), not to the Responses map.
proposed_change: Remove the header, schema and link relationships from api.responses and keep them only on api.response or api.mediatype.

subject: api.responses
text: The relationships api.responses aggregates api.schema and api.responses references api.schema largely overlap in meaning.
proposed_change: Distinguish inline schemas from $ref schemas between the two relationships, or drop one of them.

subject: api.responses
text: The associated-with relationship from api.responses to api.ratelimit is indirect; rate limiting is better attached to the operation or to a 429 Response.
proposed_change: Move the rate limit association from api.responses to api.operation or to api.response (429).

subject: api.schema
text: The relationship api.schema references api.operation has no native OpenAPI 3.0 basis, since schemas do not point to operations except via vendor extensions.
proposed_change: Remove the references relationship from api.schema to api.operation.

subject: api.schema
text: The relationship api.schema references api.tag has no native OpenAPI 3.0 basis, since schemas do not point to tags except via vendor extensions.
proposed_change: Remove the references relationship from api.schema to api.tag.

subject: api.schema
text: The relationships api.schema references api.schema and api.schema specializes api.schema overlap because both are expressed through $ref.
proposed_change: Restrict specializes to allOf inheritance/discriminator usage, leaving plain $ref to references.

subject: api.schema
text: The api.schema maps-to relationships to data-store.collection and data-store.field overlap with property-level mapping.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: api.securityscheme
text: The four references edges from api.securityscheme to application and business elements (applicationcomponent, applicationservice, businessinterface, businessservice) are vague in meaning.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: api.securityscheme
text: The uses edge from api.securityscheme to technology.systemsoftware likely overlaps with the references edge to application.applicationcomponent.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: api.securityscheme
text: The maps-to edge from api.securityscheme to security.actor misuses a schema-mapping predicate.
proposed_change: Replace maps-to with authenticates for the edge to security.actor.

subject: api.securityscheme
text: The maps-to edge from api.securityscheme to data-store.collection misuses a schema-mapping predicate.
proposed_change: Replace maps-to with accesses for the edge to data-store.collection.

subject: api.securityscheme
text: The implements edge from api.securityscheme to security.securitypolicy overstates the relationship because a scheme covers authentication only.
proposed_change: Replace implements with supports or enforces.

subject: api.securityscheme
text: The satisfies edge from api.securityscheme to motivation.principle conflicts with the Principle definition, which says it is not directly verifiable.
proposed_change: Replace satisfies with governed-by-principles.

subject: api.server
text: The relationship api.server aggregates api.servervariable should use composes, since server variables have no existence outside their server.
proposed_change: Replace aggregates with composes for server to servervariable.

subject: api.server
text: The relationship api.server references api.securityscheme is not an OpenAPI construct, because security requirements attach to the root or operations, not to servers.
proposed_change: Remove the references relationship from api.server to api.securityscheme.

subject: api.server
text: The relationship api.server satisfies security.securitypolicy is weak for a mere URL declaration.
proposed_change: Remove the satisfies relationship from api.server to security.securitypolicy.

subject: api.server
text: The relationship api.server serves application.applicationcomponent has an inverted direction, since the component is exposed via the server.
proposed_change: Reverse the direction so the application component is served/exposed via the server, or use a predicate that fits.

subject: api.server
text: The relationship api.server serves api.pathitem overlaps with plain structural scoping already expressed by the pathitem aggregating servers.
proposed_change: Remove the serves relationship from api.server to api.pathitem.

subject: api.servervariable
text: The relationship api.servervariable --[governs]--> api.server understates the link, since a server variable is structurally part of its server and cannot exist without it, so 'composes' would fit better.
proposed_change: Replace the 'governs' predicate with 'composes' for the servervariable-to-server relationship.

subject: api.servervariable
text: The relationship api.servervariable --[references]--> api.example is questionable because the OpenAPI ServerVariable object has no examples field, so it depends on vendor extensions.
proposed_change: Remove the references relationship from api.servervariable to api.example.

subject: api.servervariable
text: The relationship api.servervariable --[serves]--> api.operation only holds indirectly through api.server and may be redundant.
proposed_change: Remove the serves relationship from api.servervariable to api.operation.

subject: api.tag
text: The relationships api.tag --aggregates--> api.operation and api.tag --serves--> api.operation express the same fact (the operation lists the tag name), so they are redundant.
proposed_change: Keep only the aggregates relationship and remove serves from api.tag to api.operation.

subject: api.tag
text: The 'serves' predicate for api.tag to api.operation is semantically weak because tags provide no behavior.
proposed_change: Remove the serves relationship from api.tag to api.operation.

subject: api.tag
text: The associated-with relationships from api.tag to api.schema and api.securityscheme are indirect, derived via operations, and likely redundant.
proposed_change: Remove the associated-with relationships from api.tag to api.schema and api.securityscheme.

subject: apm.alert
text: The relationships apm.alert monitors api.operation and apm.alert monitors api.ratelimit are indirect, since alerts evaluate telemetry (spans, metrics, logs) describing these API elements, so they may be redundant with span/metric monitoring plus span-to-operation traceability.
proposed_change: Consider removing apm.alert monitors api.operation and apm.alert monitors api.ratelimit in favor of alert-to-span/metric monitoring plus span-to-operation traceability.

subject: apm.alert
text: The predicate 'monitors' on apm.alert relationships may not fit rule-over-telemetry semantics, and 'evaluates' might fit better.
proposed_change: Consider renaming the 'monitors' predicate to 'evaluates' for alert relationships to telemetry.

subject: apm.dashboard
text: The relationship apm.dashboard --[monitors]--> api.operation is indirect: dashboards observe telemetry (spans, metrics) about the operation rather than the API contract itself.
proposed_change: Replace the monitors predicate to api.operation with a weaker predicate such as references or associated-with, or remove it in favor of the telemetry relationships.

subject: apm.dashboard
text: The relationship apm.dashboard --[monitors]--> api.operation overlaps with the dashboard's monitors relationships to apm.span and apm.metricinstrument, which already capture the telemetry about the operation.
proposed_change: Drop or consolidate the api.operation relationship given the span and metricinstrument monitors relationships.

subject: apm.dashboard
text: The predicate monitors for apm.dashboard to apm.alert does not fit, because the dashboard displays alert state rather than observing a running system; references or associated-with is closer.
proposed_change: Change the predicate from monitors to references or associated-with for the dashboard-to-alert relationship.

subject: apm.exporterconfig
text: The relationship apm.exporterconfig serves data-store.database is inverted: the exporter writes to the database, so depends-on or flows-to would fit better than serves.
proposed_change: Replace the serves relationship to data-store.database with flows-to or depends-on.

subject: apm.exporterconfig
text: The relationship apm.exporterconfig serves apm.resource is questionable because providers attach the Resource and the exporter merely transports it, so associated-with may fit better.
proposed_change: Replace the serves relationship to apm.resource with associated-with.

subject: apm.exporterconfig
text: The relationship apm.exporterconfig satisfies security.retentionpolicy is weak because the backend, not the exporter, enforces retention.
proposed_change: Remove the satisfies relationship to security.retentionpolicy.

subject: apm.instrumentationconfig
text: The relationship apm.instrumentationconfig references apm.exporterconfig conflicts with the type's definition, which excludes where telemetry is sent; the link is only indirect via providers.
proposed_change: Remove the references relationship from apm.instrumentationconfig to apm.exporterconfig.

subject: apm.instrumentationconfig
text: The relationship apm.instrumentationconfig serves apm.resource is weak because the Resource is per-process and attached by providers, not served by an instrumentation entry.
proposed_change: Remove the serves relationship from apm.instrumentationconfig to apm.resource.

subject: apm.instrumentationconfig
text: The relationship apm.instrumentationconfig serves apm.instrumentationscope uses a predicate that does not fit; 'uses' or 'generates' is closer than 'serves'.
proposed_change: Replace the serves predicate with 'uses' or 'generates' for the relationship to apm.instrumentationscope.

subject: apm.instrumentationscope
text: The relationship apm.instrumentationscope aggregates apm.exporterconfig is questionable because exporters attach to providers or pipelines rather than scopes, so the link is only indirect.
proposed_change: Remove or rework the aggregates link from apm.instrumentationscope to apm.exporterconfig, since exporters attach to providers or pipelines.

subject: apm.logconfiguration
text: The relationship apm.logconfiguration serves apm.resource inverts the natural direction and conflicts with the depends-on relationship to apm.resource, since the resource serves the configuration rather than the reverse.
proposed_change: Remove the serves relationship from apm.logconfiguration to apm.resource and keep depends-on.

subject: apm.logconfiguration
text: The flows-to and aggregates relationships from apm.logconfiguration to apm.exporterconfig overlap in meaning.
proposed_change: Keep only one of flows-to or aggregates between logconfiguration and exporterconfig.

subject: apm.logconfiguration
text: The depends-on relationship from apm.logconfiguration to data-store.database duplicates what should be expressed through exporterconfig.
proposed_change: Remove the depends-on database relationship and express the dependency via exporterconfig.

subject: apm.logconfiguration
text: The monitors relationship from apm.logconfiguration to business.businessservice skips layers, because logs observe application components rather than business services.
proposed_change: Remove the monitors relationship to business.businessservice or retarget it to an application component.

subject: apm.logprocessor
text: The relationship apm.logprocessor flows-to apm.span is doubtful because log records carry span context for correlation rather than flowing into spans, so 'references' would fit better unless log-to-span-event bridging is intended.
proposed_change: Replace the flows-to predicate with 'references' (or remove it) unless log-to-span-event bridging is intended.

subject: apm.logprocessor
text: The relationship apm.logprocessor satisfies security.securityconstraints is a weak fit because separation and binding of duty are workflow rules a log processor cannot fulfil; only NeedToKnow-driven redaction plausibly applies.
proposed_change: Narrow or remove the satisfies relationship so it only covers NeedToKnow-driven redaction.

subject: apm.logrecord
text: The 'references' relationships from apm.logrecord to objectschema, schemadefinition, route, view and span are loosely typed and carry little specific meaning.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: apm.logrecord
text: Correlation of apm.logrecord to apm.span is a core OTel trace-context link and may merit a dedicated predicate instead of the generic 'references'.
proposed_change: Introduce a dedicated span-correlation predicate (e.g. correlates-with) for logrecord to span.

subject: apm.logrecord
text: The 'references' relationships from apm.logrecord to data-model.objectschema and data-model.schemadefinition overlap heavily in meaning.
proposed_change: Consolidate the two relationships into one, or define a clear distinction between them.

subject: apm.logrecord
text: The 'monitors' relationship from apm.logrecord to application.applicationservice is a weak fit, since a single log record records events rather than actively observing a service.
proposed_change: Replace or remove the 'monitors' predicate for logrecord to applicationservice, e.g. with a weaker predicate like 'references' or 'emitted-by'.

subject: apm.metricconfiguration
text: The relationship apm.metricconfiguration --serves--> apm.resource is semantically inverted, since the resource is a passive identity input consumed by the MeterProvider rather than a consumer served by it.
proposed_change: Drop the serves relationship from apm.metricconfiguration to apm.resource.

subject: apm.metricconfiguration
text: The relationship apm.metricconfiguration --serves--> apm.resource is redundant with apm.metricconfiguration --depends-on--> apm.resource, as both express the same meaning.
proposed_change: Remove serves.apm.resource and keep depends-on.apm.resource.

subject: apm.metricconfiguration
text: The relationship apm.metricconfiguration --aggregates--> apm.metricinstrument conflicts with the source definition, which says the configuration is 'not any individual instrument', so aggregation is the wrong predicate.
proposed_change: Replace the aggregates predicate with a governs/applies-style predicate.

subject: apm.metricinstrument
text: The relationship apm.metricinstrument flows-to apm.logprocessor is semantically wrong because metrics flow to readers or exporters, not to log processors.
proposed_change: Remove the flows-to relationship from apm.metricinstrument to apm.logprocessor.

subject: apm.metricinstrument
text: The relationship apm.metricinstrument flows-to apm.span is semantically wrong because metrics flow to readers or exporters, not to spans, and exemplar links are already covered by references span.
proposed_change: Remove the flows-to relationship from apm.metricinstrument to apm.span and rely on references span for exemplar links.

subject: apm.metricinstrument
text: The relationship apm.metricinstrument realizes motivation.goal uses a predicate that does not fit; it should be supports-goals.
proposed_change: Replace the realizes predicate with supports-goals for the relationship to motivation.goal.

subject: apm.metricinstrument
text: The relationship apm.metricinstrument maps-to motivation.outcome uses a predicate that does not fit; it should be measures-outcome.
proposed_change: Replace the maps-to predicate with measures-outcome for the relationship to motivation.outcome.

subject: apm.metricinstrument
text: The relationship apm.metricinstrument monitors api.pathitem is redundant with monitors api.operation.
proposed_change: Remove the monitors relationship to api.pathitem and keep the one to api.operation.

subject: apm.metricinstrument
text: The monitors relationships from apm.metricinstrument to ux.errorconfig, security.threat, data-model.objectschema and data-model.schemadefinition are only indirect at best.
proposed_change: Remove these indirect monitors relationships from apm.metricinstrument.

subject: apm.resource
text: The relationships apm.resource monitors technology.node and technology.systemsoftware use the wrong predicate, since a Resource passively identifies its host or runtime rather than observing it.
proposed_change: Replace monitors with references or associated-with for Node and SystemSoftware.

subject: apm.resource
text: The relationship apm.resource serves business.businessprocess is dubious because a Resource is an attribute set and does not serve a business process.
proposed_change: Remove the serves relationship to BusinessProcess.

subject: apm.resource
text: The relationship apm.resource aggregates apm.exporterconfig is questionable because exporters belong to providers, not to the Resource.
proposed_change: Remove the aggregates relationship to ExporterConfig.

subject: apm.resource
text: The relationship apm.resource references security.secureresource is weak and overlaps with the maps-to relationship to application.applicationcomponent.
proposed_change: Remove the references relationship to SecureResource and keep maps-to ApplicationComponent.

subject: apm.span
text: The relationship apm.span composes apm.metricinstrument is questionable because metric instruments exist independently of spans.
proposed_change: Replace composes with a generates or measures relationship between span and metricinstrument.

subject: apm.span
text: The relationship apm.span composes apm.traceconfiguration is inverted because a trace configuration governs many spans rather than being owned by one span.
proposed_change: Replace with a governed-by relationship from span to traceconfiguration.

subject: apm.span
text: The relationship apm.span flows-to apm.logprocessor is a weak cross-signal path.
proposed_change: Remove the span flows-to logprocessor relationship.

subject: apm.span
text: The relationship apm.span references apm.span duplicates the apm.span aggregates apm.spanlink relationship in meaning.
proposed_change: Remove the span references span relationship, keeping aggregates spanlink.

subject: apm.span
text: The relationship apm.span monitors data-model.objectschema is a stretch because spans observe operations, not schemas.
proposed_change: Remove the span monitors objectschema relationship.

subject: apm.spanevent
text: The depends-on relationships from apm.spanevent to apm.instrumentationscope and apm.resource are indirect, because both attach to the parent span or batch rather than to the event, so the semantics should be 'inherits via span'.
proposed_change: Remove these direct depends-on links or replace them with an 'inherits via span' relationship.

subject: apm.spanevent
text: The monitors relationship from apm.spanevent to ux.actioncomponent is doubtful because a span event records an occurrence rather than observing a UI control.
proposed_change: Remove the monitors relationship to ux.actioncomponent.

subject: apm.spanevent
text: The triggers relationship from apm.spanevent to apm.metricinstrument is usually co-emission rather than causation, so the predicate does not fit.
proposed_change: Remove the triggers relationship or replace it with a predicate expressing co-emission.

subject: apm.spanlink
text: The apm.spanlink references apm.span relationship points at a span element that is a code-location definition rather than a runtime occurrence, so the link actually refers to the span definition whose runtime instances it targets; the semantics of this relationship need clarification.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: apm.spanlink
text: Ownership of a span link by its carrier span (a composed-of relationship from apm.span to apm.spanlink) is not covered by the existing relationships, and may need a separate composes relationship, since the current one is an aggregates relationship.
proposed_change: Add a separate composition relationship from apm.span to apm.spanlink to express carrier ownership.

subject: apm.traceconfiguration
text: The aggregates relationship from apm.traceconfiguration to apm.metricinstrument is questionable because TraceConfiguration governs a TracerProvider, not a MeterProvider.
proposed_change: Remove the aggregates relationship from apm.traceconfiguration to apm.metricinstrument.

subject: apm.traceconfiguration
text: The satisfies relationship from apm.traceconfiguration to security.securitypolicy is a weak fit because an XACML-style access-decision policy is not something a tracing config satisfies.
proposed_change: Replace the satisfies predicate with constrained-by or governed-by for the link to security.securitypolicy.

subject: apm.traceconfiguration
text: The monitors relationships from apm.traceconfiguration to application.applicationservice and to business.businessservice overlap with each other.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: apm.traceconfiguration
text: The depends-on relationship from apm.traceconfiguration to data-store.database is indirect, since the dependency really sits with the tracing backend.
proposed_change: Remove the depends-on Database relationship, or move the dependency to the backend.

subject: application.applicationcollaboration
text: The delivers-value relationships from application.applicationcollaboration to application.applicationinteraction and application.applicationservice use a traceability predicate, whereas ArchiMate would use assigned-to for collaboration to interaction and realizes for collaboration to service.
proposed_change: Replace delivers-value with assigned-to for collaboration to interaction and with realizes for collaboration to service.

subject: application.applicationcollaboration
text: The depends-on relationship from application.applicationcollaboration to application.applicationcomponent overlaps with the aggregates relationship to the same target when the target is a member of the collaboration.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: application.applicationcollaboration
text: The depends-on relationship from application.applicationcollaboration to application.applicationinteraction partly inverts the performer relationship, since the interaction is performed by the collaboration.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: application.applicationcollaboration
text: The provides relationship from application.applicationcollaboration to application.applicationinterface conflicts with the interface definition, which says an interface is owned by a component.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: application.applicationcomponent
text: The relationships assigned-to and composes from application.applicationcomponent to application.applicationfunction overlap in meaning.
proposed_change: Keep only assigned-to for component-to-function and remove the redundant composes relationship.

subject: application.applicationcomponent
text: The composes relationship from application.applicationcomponent to application.applicationfunction, composition between active structure and behaviour, is not valid in ArchiMate.
proposed_change: Remove the composes relationship from ApplicationComponent to ApplicationFunction.

subject: application.applicationcomponent
text: The relationships assigned-to and provides from application.applicationcomponent to application.applicationinterface are redundant, since ArchiMate uses composition for component-to-interface.
proposed_change: Remove the assigned-to and provides relationships and use a single composes relationship from ApplicationComponent to ApplicationInterface.

subject: application.applicationcomponent
text: ApplicationComponent realizing motivation.goal and motivation.principle directly is questionable, because core elements normally realize Requirements, which in turn realize goals and principles.
proposed_change: Remove the direct realizes relationships to Goal and Principle and route them through Requirement.

subject: application.applicationevent
text: The relationship application.applicationevent triggers application.applicationcollaboration is semantically wrong because in ArchiMate triggers links behaviour elements while a collaboration is active structure.
proposed_change: Replace the triggers relationship to ApplicationCollaboration with a triggers relationship from ApplicationEvent to ApplicationInteraction.

subject: application.applicationevent
text: The ApplicationEvent depends-on DataObject relationship is loose for expressing an event payload; associated-with, or access via the handling process, would be more accurate.
proposed_change: Replace depends-on toward DataObject with associated-with, or model payload access through the handling process.

subject: application.applicationfunction
text: The delivers-value relationship from application.applicationfunction to application.applicationservice largely duplicates the realizes relationship between the same two types.
proposed_change: Remove the delivers-value relationship to ApplicationService and keep realizes.

subject: application.applicationfunction
text: The depends-on relationship from application.applicationfunction to application.dataobject overlaps with the accesses relationship between the same two types.
proposed_change: Remove the depends-on relationship to DataObject and keep accesses.

subject: application.applicationfunction
text: The delivers-value predicate is a traceability predicate meant for business value, so using it from application.applicationfunction to application.applicationprocess is questionable.
proposed_change: Replace delivers-value with consumed-by or serves for the relationship to ApplicationProcess.

subject: application.applicationinteraction
text: The delivers-value relationship from application.applicationinteraction to application.applicationservice is redundant with the realizes relationship between the same pair, and delivers-value is a traceability predicate meant for business value/goals, so it is misused here.
proposed_change: Remove the delivers-value relationship from ApplicationInteraction to ApplicationService and keep realizes.

subject: application.applicationinteraction
text: The depends-on relationship from application.applicationinteraction to application.applicationcollaboration inverts ArchiMate semantics, because the collaboration should be assigned to the interaction.
proposed_change: Replace it with an assigned-to relationship from ApplicationCollaboration to ApplicationInteraction.

subject: application.applicationinteraction
text: The depends-on relationship from application.applicationinteraction to application.dataobject is imprecise and would be better expressed as accesses.
proposed_change: Change the predicate from depends-on to accesses.

subject: application.applicationinterface
text: The relationship ApplicationInterface delivers-value to ApplicationCollaboration is odd because delivers-value is a traceability value predicate targeting an active-structure grouping; aggregation or assignment fits better.
proposed_change: Replace delivers-value from ApplicationInterface to ApplicationCollaboration with an aggregation or assignment relationship.

subject: application.applicationinterface
text: ApplicationInterface depends-on ApplicationComponent inverts ArchiMate composition, in which the component is composed of the interface.
proposed_change: Reverse it to a component-to-interface composition (component composed-of interface) or drop the depends-on.

subject: application.applicationinterface
text: ApplicationInterface depends-on ApplicationService and ApplicationInterface serves ApplicationService overlap in meaning.
proposed_change: Consolidate the two into a single relationship between ApplicationInterface and ApplicationService.

subject: application.applicationinterface
text: ApplicationInterface serves ApplicationService inverts ArchiMate, where the service is exposed through or assigned to the interface.
proposed_change: Reverse the direction so the service is assigned to or exposed through the interface, or remove the serves relationship.

subject: application.applicationprocess
text: The delivers-value relationship from application.applicationprocess to application.applicationservice uses a business-value traceability predicate, whereas process-to-service is classically ArchiMate realizes.
proposed_change: Replace delivers-value with realizes for ApplicationProcess to ApplicationService.

subject: application.applicationprocess
text: The depends-on and triggers relationships between application.applicationprocess and application.applicationevent have unclear direction, since it is ambiguous whether they mean an inbound trigger or an emission.
proposed_change: Clarify the semantics so that inbound triggering is distinguished from event emission, and remove the overlapping depends-on.

subject: application.applicationprocess
text: The depends-on relationship from application.applicationprocess to application.applicationcollaboration inverts ArchiMate assignment, in which the collaboration is assigned to the process.
proposed_change: Reverse the direction to collaboration assigned-to process, or replace the depends-on with an assignment-style relationship.

subject: application.applicationprocess
text: The depends-on relationship from application.applicationprocess to application.dataobject would be more precise as accesses.
proposed_change: Replace depends-on with accesses for ApplicationProcess to DataObject.

subject: application.applicationservice
text: The relationships application.applicationservice accesses application.dataobject and application.applicationservice depends-on application.dataobject overlap in meaning.
proposed_change: Remove or clearly differentiate one of the accesses/depends-on relationships to DataObject.

subject: application.applicationservice
text: The relationship application.applicationservice realizes motivation.goal uses a non-standard predicate; supports or supports-goals fits better.
proposed_change: Replace the realizes predicate to Goal with supports (supports-goals).

subject: application.applicationservice
text: The ApplicationService relationship realizes Requirement and satisfies Constraint use inconsistent predicates for similar traceability to motivation elements.
proposed_change: Harmonize the predicates used for Requirement and Constraint traceability.

subject: application.applicationservice
text: The relationships application.applicationservice flows-to application.applicationservice and depends-on application.applicationservice may duplicate each other.
proposed_change: Merge or clearly differentiate flows-to and depends-on between services.

subject: application.applicationservice
text: ApplicationService serving motivation.stakeholder is odd because a stakeholder is a motivation element rather than an actor or role.
proposed_change: Replace the serves relationship to Stakeholder with one targeting a role or actor.

subject: application.applicationservice
text: The constrained-by relationship to security.accesscondition is too fine-grained for ApplicationService.
proposed_change: Constrain the service via a security policy rule instead of AccessCondition.

subject: application.dataobject
text: The direction of the 'composes' relationship from application.dataobject to application.dataobject is ambiguous: its inverse 'composed-of' implies the source is the part, whereas ArchiMate and the parallel 'aggregates' relationship make the source the whole.
proposed_change: Clarify and document that the source of 'composes' is the whole (aligned with ArchiMate and 'aggregates'), and make the inverse name 'composed-of' consistent with that.

subject: application.dataobject
text: The 'realizes' relationship between data objects overlaps with 'specializes' and 'extends' for interface or abstract-type implementation, so a precedence rule is needed.
proposed_change: Define a precedence rule stating when to use realizes versus specializes or extends between data objects.

subject: business.businessactor
text: The accesses relationships from business.businessactor to business objects are only shortcuts, because ArchiMate permits access only from behavior elements (or derived via roles), not directly from active structure.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: business.businessactor
text: The business.businessactor accesses business.contract relationship is largely redundant with business.businessactor accesses business.businessobject, since Contract is a specialization of BusinessObject.
proposed_change: Remove the accesses relationship from business.businessactor to business.contract and rely on the one to business.businessobject.

subject: business.businessactor
text: The business.businessactor serves motivation.stakeholder relationship is semantically weak: Stakeholder is a motivation element, ArchiMate allows only association there, and an actor often simply is the stakeholder.
proposed_change: Remove or replace the serves relationship to motivation.stakeholder (e.g., with association).

subject: business.businesscollaboration
text: The composes relationship from business.businesscollaboration to business.businessrole conflicts with ArchiMate semantics because roles exist independently of any collaboration, so it should be aggregation rather than composition.
proposed_change: Replace the composes relationship with an aggregates relationship from BusinessCollaboration to BusinessRole.

subject: business.businesscollaboration
text: The accesses relationship from business.businesscollaboration to business.businessobject is a derived shortcut, since in ArchiMate access normally belongs to the BusinessInteraction the collaboration performs rather than to the active structure itself.
proposed_change: Remove the direct accesses relationship and model access on BusinessInteraction instead.

subject: business.businessevent
text: The triggers relationship from business.businessevent to business.businessfunction is semantically weak because a BusinessFunction has no defined start or sequence, so it should be read as initiating behavior within the function rather than starting the function itself.
proposed_change: Document that the event triggers behavior within the function, or model the triggered behavior as a process the function contains instead of triggering the function directly.

subject: business.businessfunction
text: The relationship business.businessfunction realizes motivation.goal is questionable because ArchiMate lets core elements realize requirements and influence goals, so 'supports' or 'influence' fits better.
proposed_change: Replace the realizes predicate to motivation.goal with 'supports' or 'influences'.

subject: business.businessfunction
text: The composes self-relationship on business.businessfunction has ambiguous direction (whole vs. part as source) and is not documented explicitly.
proposed_change: Document explicitly which end (whole or part) is the source of the composes relationship.

subject: business.businessfunction
text: The relationship business.businessfunction serves business.businessrole is valid but weak, since roles are typically assigned to functions rather than served by them.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: business.businessinteraction
text: The relationship 'business.businessinteraction serves business.businessservice' is semantically off, because in ArchiMate a business interaction realizes a business service and the service then serves consumers.
proposed_change: Replace the 'serves' relationship from BusinessInteraction to BusinessService with a 'realizes' relationship.

subject: business.businessinteraction
text: If a 'realizes' relationship from business.businessinteraction to business.businessservice exists or is intended, the 'serves' relationship between the same pair is redundant with it.
proposed_change: Remove the 'serves' relationship from BusinessInteraction to BusinessService if a 'realizes' relationship is added.

subject: business.businessinteraction
text: The business.businessinteraction relationship catalog has no 'realizes' relationship to business.businessservice, which ArchiMate typically uses for an interaction delivering a service.
proposed_change: Add a 'realizes' relationship from business.businessinteraction to business.businessservice.

subject: business.businessinterface
text: The flows-to relationship from business.businessinterface to business.businessobject is non-standard ArchiMate, since flow links behavior or active elements rather than passive objects, and it largely duplicates the accesses relationship.
proposed_change: Remove the flows-to relationship from business.businessinterface to business.businessobject and keep accesses.

subject: business.businessinterface
text: The triggers relationships from business.businessinterface to behavior elements are not valid ArchiMate, because triggering holds between behaviors or events, not from an interface.
proposed_change: Remove the triggers relationships from business.businessinterface or replace them with serves or assigned-to via the service.

subject: business.businessinterface
text: The triggers relationship from business.businessinterface to business.businessfunction is especially doubtful because a BusinessFunction has no defined start.
proposed_change: Replace it with serves, or with assigned-to via the service.

subject: business.businessobject
text: The relationship business.businessobject --[references]--> application.dataobject is too weak, because ArchiMate models the link as the data object realizing the business object.
proposed_change: Replace the references relationship from business object to data object with an inverse realizes relationship (application.dataobject realizes business.businessobject).

subject: business.businessprocess
text: The relationships business.businessprocess accesses BusinessObject and business.businessprocess delivers BusinessObject overlap in meaning; delivers suits outcome/value targets, whereas ArchiMate would use access (write).
proposed_change: Remove or redefine delivers on BusinessObject and use accesses (write) as ArchiMate does.

subject: business.businessprocess
text: The cross-layer relationship business.businessprocess aggregates application.applicationprocess has questionable direction/semantics, since ArchiMate normally has an application process serving or realizing the business process.
proposed_change: Replace the aggregates relationship with application process serving or realizing the business process.

subject: business.businessprocess
text: The relationship business.businessprocess realizes motivation.goal skips the Outcome/Requirement chain and overlaps with realizes Outcome and satisfies Requirement.
proposed_change: Remove realizes Goal and route goal contribution through Outcome and Requirement.

subject: business.businessprocess
text: The flows-to and triggers relationships between business processes are distinct but often conflated, so their semantics need to be kept clear.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: business.businessrole
text: BusinessRole assigned-to BusinessFunction and BusinessRole performs BusinessFunction express the same meaning, since ArchiMate expresses both via Assignment.
proposed_change: Remove one of the two relationships (likely performs) and keep a single assignment relationship from BusinessRole to BusinessFunction.

subject: business.businessrole
text: BusinessRole assigned-to BusinessProcess and BusinessRole performs BusinessProcess express the same meaning, since ArchiMate expresses both via Assignment.
proposed_change: Remove one of the two relationships (likely performs) and keep a single assignment relationship from BusinessRole to BusinessProcess.

subject: business.businessrole
text: BusinessRole assigned-to BusinessInterface has the wrong direction compared with ArchiMate, where the interface is assigned to the role or the role composes the interface.
proposed_change: Reverse the direction to BusinessInterface assigned-to BusinessRole, or replace it with BusinessRole composes BusinessInterface.

subject: business.businessrole
text: BusinessRole serves Stakeholder crosses the business and motivation layers loosely, and association is a better-fitting predicate.
proposed_change: Replace the serves relationship with an association between BusinessRole and Stakeholder.

subject: business.businessrole
text: BusinessRole triggers BusinessEvent is non-standard in ArchiMate.
proposed_change: Remove the triggers relationship from BusinessRole to BusinessEvent.

subject: business.businessservice
text: The relationship business.businessservice realizes business.businessprocess is inverted, since in ArchiMate processes realize services, and the reverse relationship business.businessprocess realizes business.businessservice already exists.
proposed_change: Remove or invert the businessservice realizes businessprocess relationship, keeping businessprocess realizes businessservice.

subject: business.contract
text: The relationship business.contract accesses business.businessobject is invalid because accesses must originate from behavior, not from a passive object like Contract; it was likely meant as associated-with or aggregates.
proposed_change: Replace the accesses relationship from contract to businessobject with associated-with or aggregates.

subject: business.contract
text: The relationship business.contract triggers business.businessprocess is invalid because a passive object cannot trigger; triggers should originate from a BusinessEvent such as 'Contract Signed'.
proposed_change: Remove the triggers relationship from contract and have businessevent trigger the process instead.

subject: business.contract
text: The relationship business.contract serves business.businessrole is invalid because a passive object cannot serve; it could be expressed as associated-with.
proposed_change: Replace serves with associated-with between contract and businessrole.

subject: business.contract
text: The relationship business.contract governs business.businessservice is appropriate for a Contract.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: business.representation
text: The relationship business.representation realizes business.contract is technically redundant because Contract is a specialization of BusinessObject, so it is subsumed by the realizes relationship to business.businessobject, and is kept only for explicitness.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: data-model.arrayschema
text: The aggregates relationships from data-model.arrayschema to data-model.reference and to data-model.schemadefinition overlap, because an items $ref is a Reference that resolves to a SchemaDefinition, so both edges may be recorded for a single link.
proposed_change: Model ArraySchema→Reference and Reference→SchemaDefinition instead of a direct ArraySchema→SchemaDefinition aggregates edge.

subject: data-model.arrayschema
text: The maps-to relationship from data-model.arrayschema to api.response uses a data-layer predicate, and describing a response body may fit a 'references' or 'used-by' relation better.
proposed_change: Replace the maps-to predicate with 'references' or 'used-by' for the arrayschema to api.response relationship.

subject: data-model.jsonschema
text: The realizes relationship from data-model.jsonschema to motivation.goal is weak because a data schema rarely realizes a goal directly; a supports/supports-goals predicate fits better.
proposed_change: Replace realizes with supports (supports-goals) for the relationship to motivation.goal.

subject: data-model.jsonschema
text: The realizes relationship from data-model.jsonschema to api.schema could equally be expressed as maps-to.
proposed_change: Consider changing realizes to maps-to for the relationship to api.schema.

subject: data-model.jsonschema
text: The serves relationships from data-model.jsonschema to application.applicationfunction and business.businessservice are indirect, since passive schemas are accessed rather than serving.
proposed_change: Replace or reconsider the serves predicate, e.g. use an access-style relationship; none more specific stated.

subject: data-model.jsonschema
text: The depends-on relationship to technology.systemsoftware overlaps with the uses relationship to technology.technologyservice.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: data-model.objectschema
text: The relationship data-model.objectschema realizes motivation.goal is dubious because data structures rarely realize goals directly; a supports relationship would fit better.
proposed_change: Replace the realizes relationship to motivation.goal with a supports relationship.

subject: data-model.objectschema
text: The relationships data-model.objectschema realizes business.businessobject and data-model.objectschema realizes application.dataobject partially overlap in meaning.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: data-model.objectschema
text: The relationship data-model.objectschema satisfies security.securityconstraints is weak because the security constraints container holds procedural rules, which an object schema does not satisfy.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: data-model.objectschema
text: The relationships data-model.objectschema serves application.applicationcomponent and data-model.objectschema serves application.applicationfunction are redundant with the inverse of the component's or function's uses or accesses relationship to the object schema.
proposed_change: Remove the serves relationships and rely on the inverse of the uses or accesses relationships from the application component and function.

subject: data-model.reference
text: The relationship data-model.reference maps-to application.applicationservice looks misplaced because a $ref adds no content of its own, so any service mapping belongs on the SchemaDefinition it resolves to.
proposed_change: Remove the maps-to relationship from data-model.reference to application.applicationservice and place the service mapping on data-model.schemadefinition.

subject: data-model.reference
text: The relationship data-model.reference maps-to api.schema is less strongly misplaced because it duplicates what the resolved SchemaDefinition would map to.
proposed_change: Remove or reconsider the maps-to relationship from data-model.reference to api.schema, relying on the mapping of the resolved data-model.schemadefinition.

subject: data-model.schemacomposition
text: The 'composes' relationship from data-model.schemacomposition to data-model.schemadefinition is questionable because a named definition exists independently and is reused via $ref, so composition's lifecycle ownership does not fit.
proposed_change: Replace 'composes' with 'aggregates' or 'references' for the relationship to data-model.schemadefinition.

subject: data-model.schemacomposition
text: The 'serves' relationship from data-model.schemacomposition to application.applicationfunction is odd because 'serves' is a behavioral predicate and a schema composition is a passive structure.
proposed_change: Replace 'serves' with 'used-by' (the inverse of uses) or an ArchiMate access relationship from the application function to the schema composition.

subject: data-model.schemadefinition
text: The serves relationships from data-model.schemadefinition to application.applicationcomponent, application.applicationfunction and api.operation overlap with the more precise realizes link to application.dataobject and maps-to link to api.schema.
proposed_change: Remove the serves relationships to application component, application function and api operation in favour of realizes→dataobject and maps-to→api.schema.

subject: data-model.schemadefinition
text: The requires relationship from data-model.schemadefinition to security.retentionpolicy is a poor fit because that policy covers security data such as audit logs rather than domain types.
proposed_change: Remove the requires relationship to security.retentionpolicy.

subject: data-model.schemadefinition
text: The satisfies predicate from data-model.schemadefinition to security.dataclassification fits poorly and governed-by or constrained-by would read better.
proposed_change: Replace the satisfies predicate with governed-by or constrained-by for the link to security.dataclassification.

subject: data-model.schemaproperty
text: The five 'references' relationships from data-model.schemaproperty to arrayschema, numericschema, objectschema, schemadefinition and stringschema treat the property's own value subschema as a separate referenced element, although the property has no meaning apart from it, so 'composes' or a typed-by predicate may fit better.
proposed_change: Replace the 'references' predicate on these five relationships with 'composes' or a typed-by style predicate.

subject: data-model.schemaproperty
text: The relationship data-model.schemaproperty satisfies security.validationrule overlaps with the references relationships to stringschema and numericschema, since both express the same value restrictions.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: data-store.accesspattern
text: The relationship data-store.accesspattern aggregates data-store.collection duplicates accesses and misuses whole-part semantics, since an access pattern targets rather than contains a collection.
proposed_change: Remove the aggregates relationship from accesspattern to collection and keep accesses.

subject: data-store.accesspattern
text: The relationship data-store.accesspattern aggregates data-store.index overlaps with the uses relationship to index, and uses is the correct predicate.
proposed_change: Remove the aggregates relationship from accesspattern to index and keep uses.

subject: data-store.accesspattern
text: The relationship data-store.accesspattern aggregates data-store.field is better expressed with the references predicate.
proposed_change: Replace aggregates with references for accesspattern to field.

subject: data-store.accesspattern
text: The relationship data-store.accesspattern satisfies security.accesscondition is semantically odd, because access conditions are evaluated by policy checks, not realized by queries.
proposed_change: Remove the satisfies relationship from accesspattern to security.accesscondition.

subject: data-store.accesspattern
text: The relationship data-store.accesspattern serves business.businessfunction skips the application layer.
proposed_change: Remove the direct serves link to businessfunction and route through application.applicationfunction.

subject: data-store.collection
text: The relationship data-store.collection composes data-store.namespace is inverted, because namespaces contain collections (a reverse namespace-composes-collection already exists).
proposed_change: Remove collection-composes-namespace and keep only namespace-composes-collection.

subject: data-store.collection
text: The relationship data-store.collection composes data-store.collection is valid only for partitions or subcollections, not for general collection nesting.
proposed_change: Restrict or document collection-composes-collection as applying only to partitions or subcollections.

subject: data-store.collection
text: The relationship data-store.collection maps-to api.requestbody overlaps with data-store.collection realizes api.schema, since request bodies are expressed through schemas.
proposed_change: Remove the maps-to api.requestbody relationship and rely on realizes api.schema.

subject: data-store.collection
text: The relationship data-store.collection implements security.secureresource could equally be expressed as realizes.
proposed_change: Consider changing the predicate from implements to realizes.

subject: data-store.collection
text: The relationships data-store.collection serves application.applicationcomponent and data-store.collection serves application.applicationservice partly duplicate each other.
proposed_change: Consolidate the two serves relationships into one or clarify the distinction between them.

subject: data-store.database
text: The direct composes relationships from data-store.database to data-store.field, data-store.index and data-store.validationrule are redundant with the composition path database→namespace→collection.
proposed_change: Remove the direct composes relationships from database to field, index and validationrule.

subject: data-store.database
text: The realizes relationship from data-store.database to business.businessservice is doubtful because a data store serves rather than realizes business behavior.
proposed_change: Remove or replace the realizes relationship with a serves relationship.

subject: data-store.database
text: The satisfies relationship from data-store.database to security.securitypolicy reads better as governed-by because the database is a policy target.
proposed_change: Replace satisfies with a governed-by predicate for database to securitypolicy.

subject: data-store.database
text: The depends-on relationship to technology.systemsoftware and the uses relationship to technology.technologyservice overlap in meaning.
proposed_change: Clarify the boundary between depends-on systemsoftware and uses technologyservice, or merge them.

subject: data-store.database
text: The federates and replicates relationships from data-store.database to itself need a clear distinction from each other.
proposed_change: Document distinct semantics for federates versus replicates.

subject: data-store.eventhandler
text: The relationship data-store.eventhandler --[triggers]--> business.businessevent crosses abstraction levels, because a data-store handler should reach a BusinessEvent only via an ApplicationEvent (handler → ApplicationEvent → realizes/flows to BusinessEvent).
proposed_change: Remove the direct triggers relationship to business.businessevent or mark it as derived/optional, relying on the path through application.applicationevent.

subject: data-store.field
text: The relationship data-store.field triggers data-store.validationrule uses a predicate that does not fit, because declarative constraints restrict field values rather than being initiated by them; constrained-by would model it better.
proposed_change: Replace the 'triggers' predicate with 'constrained-by' for the field to validationrule relationship.

subject: data-store.field
text: The relationship data-store.field triggers data-store.storedlogic partly duplicates the path through data-store.eventhandler, which by definition is the activation wiring that invokes stored logic.
proposed_change: Remove the direct field triggers storedlogic relationship and rely on the path through eventhandler.

subject: data-store.field
text: The relationship data-store.field satisfies security.dataclassification conflates labelling a field with complying with a classification tier; a classified-as predicate would be clearer.
proposed_change: Replace the 'satisfies' predicate with 'classified-as' for the field to dataclassification relationship.

subject: data-store.namespace
text: The relationship data-store.namespace composes data-store.field is redundant and transitive, since fields belong to collections, which already compose them.
proposed_change: Remove the namespace composes field relationship.

subject: data-store.namespace
text: The namespace composes index and namespace composes validationrule relationships partly overlap with collection-level ownership of indexes and validation rules.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: data-store.namespace
text: The relationship data-store.namespace composes data-store.namespace conflicts with the definition of a namespace as inside a single database instance, unless the engine has nested hierarchies such as catalog.schema.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: data-store.namespace
text: The relationship id for namespace composing storedlogic lacks the data-store. prefix on the target.
proposed_change: Fix the relationship id so storedlogic carries the data-store. prefix.

subject: data-store.retentionpolicy
text: The aggregates relationships from data-store.retentionpolicy to data-store.collection and data-store.namespace duplicate the governs relationships to the same targets.
proposed_change: Drop the aggregates relationships to Collection and Namespace and keep governs.

subject: data-store.retentionpolicy
text: A retention policy does not contain containers as parts but scopes and rules them, so governs is the correct predicate rather than aggregates toward Collection and Namespace.
proposed_change: Remove aggregates in favor of governs.

subject: data-store.retentionpolicy
text: The satisfies relationship from data-store.retentionpolicy to security.retentionpolicy holds only when the policy's maximum age is not shorter than the security policy's minimum retention period.
proposed_change: Document this condition on the satisfies relationship to security.retentionpolicy.

subject: data-store.storedlogic
text: The aggregates relationships from data-store.storedlogic to data-store.collection and data-store.field are dubious because stored logic references these elements but does not group them, and the accesses relationship already covers this.
proposed_change: Remove the aggregates relationships from storedlogic to collection and field, relying on accesses.

subject: data-store.storedlogic
text: The composes relationship from data-store.storedlogic to data-store.validationrule contradicts the ValidationRule definition, since a validation rule is a declarative schema constraint and not part of procedural code.
proposed_change: Remove the composes relationship from storedlogic to validationrule.

subject: data-store.storedlogic
text: The validates relationship from data-store.storedlogic to data-store.collection is a testing predicate that overlaps with accesses, and imperative triggers are excluded from ValidationRule.
proposed_change: Remove the validates relationship from storedlogic to collection, relying on accesses.

subject: data-store.storedlogic
text: The realizes relationship from data-store.storedlogic to business.businessfunction skips the application layer, so implements to application.applicationfunction is preferable.
proposed_change: Remove the realizes relationship to business.businessfunction and keep implements to application.applicationfunction.

subject: data-store.validationrule
text: The relationship data-store.validationrule cascades-to data-store.collection only makes sense for FOREIGN_KEY rules with ON DELETE/UPDATE actions, since CHECK, NOT NULL and unique rules never cascade, but it is not restricted to foreign-key rules.
proposed_change: Limit the cascades-to relationship to validation rules with ruleType FOREIGN_KEY (those with referential actions).

subject: data-store.validationrule
text: The relationship data-store.validationrule satisfies motivation.requirement overlaps with the governance predicate enforces-requirement, so constraint-to-requirement traceability has two competing predicates.
proposed_change: Pick a single predicate (either satisfies or enforces-requirement) for constraint-to-requirement traceability across the spec.

subject: data-store.view
text: The relationship data-store.view aggregates data-store.collection largely duplicates data-store.view derives-from data-store.collection, and derives-from is the more accurate semantics.
proposed_change: Remove the aggregates relationship from data-store.view to data-store.collection and keep derives-from.

subject: data-store.view
text: The relationship data-store.view aggregates data-store.field is odd because fields belong to persisted collections, not to views.
proposed_change: Remove the aggregates relationship from data-store.view to data-store.field.

subject: data-store.view
text: The relationship data-store.view realizes api.response skips the intermediate application/API layers and is weak.
proposed_change: Remove the realizes relationship from data-store.view to api.response.

subject: data-store.view
text: The relationship data-store.view serves business.businessservice skips intermediate layers and is weak, whereas serves application.applicationservice is the more defensible link.
proposed_change: Remove the serves relationship to business.businessservice and keep serves to application.applicationservice.

subject: motivation.assessment
text: The associated-with relationships from motivation.assessment to motivation.constraint and motivation.outcome are inconsistent with the influence relationships from assessment to goal, requirement and principle; an assessment shaping an outcome or constraint would likewise be influence.
proposed_change: Replace the associated-with relationships to constraint and outcome with influence relationships.

subject: motivation.assessment
text: The influence relationship from motivation.assessment to motivation.driver inverts ArchiMate's convention, where assessments are associated with the drivers they evaluate.
proposed_change: Replace the assessment-influence-driver relationship with associated-with between assessment and driver.

subject: motivation.assessment
text: The influence relationship from motivation.assessment to motivation.assessment risks overlapping with generic association.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: motivation.constraint
text: The relationships motivation.constraint --[constrains]--> motivation.requirement and motivation.constraint --[influence]--> motivation.requirement both express a constraint shaping a requirement, so modelers will struggle to choose between them.
proposed_change: Keep 'constrains' for limiting the solution space and reserve 'influence' for weaker, non-restrictive effects, or drop the influence relationship from motivation.constraint to motivation.requirement.

subject: motivation.driver
text: The associated-with relationship from motivation.driver to motivation.constraint is weak; a driver-to-constraint link is usually causal and would be better expressed as influence, as is done for goals and requirements.
proposed_change: Replace the associated-with relationship from motivation.driver to motivation.constraint with an influence relationship.

subject: motivation.driver
text: The associated-with relationship from motivation.driver to motivation.value is vague and may duplicate paths that already run through goals or outcomes.
proposed_change: Remove the driver-to-value associated-with relationship or justify it against the paths via goals or outcomes.

subject: motivation.goal
text: The relationship motivation.goal aggregates motivation.requirement inverts the usual ArchiMate direction, in which requirements realize goals.
proposed_change: Remove or reverse the goal-aggregates-requirement relationship so that requirement realizes goal is the canonical form.

subject: motivation.goal
text: The relationship motivation.goal realizes motivation.goal overlaps with motivation.goal aggregates motivation.goal and motivation.goal influence motivation.goal as variants of goal decomposition.
proposed_change: Consolidate the goal-to-goal decomposition relationships into one, with clear semantics for the rest.

subject: motivation.goal
text: The relationships motivation.goal influence motivation.principle and motivation.goal supports motivation.principle are largely redundant with each other.
proposed_change: Keep only one of influence or supports between goal and principle.

subject: motivation.goal
text: The relationship motivation.goal realizes motivation.value is unusual, and association would be more typical.
proposed_change: Replace goal realizes value with an associated-with relationship.

subject: motivation.goal
text: The relationship motivation.goal influence motivation.assessment reverses the normal direction, in which an assessment influences a goal.
