proposed_change: Remove goal influence assessment and rely on assessment influence goal.

subject: motivation.meaning
text: All six relationships from motivation.meaning use the generic associated-with predicate, which is ArchiMate's only permitted relation for Meaning but carries little semantics.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: motivation.meaning
text: The direction of the associated-with relationships from motivation.meaning is ambiguous because Meaning interprets a concept rather than the target motivation element itself.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: motivation.meaning
text: The meaning-to-stakeholder link is the most substantive (whose interpretation), while the other associations essentially only say 'defines a term used in'.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: motivation.outcome
text: The relationships motivation.outcome --influence--> motivation.goal and motivation.outcome --realizes--> motivation.goal overlap in meaning; modelers should use realizes for full attainment and influence for partial contribution.
proposed_change: Document a usage rule: realizes for full attainment of the goal, influence for partial contribution (or merge the two).

subject: motivation.outcome
text: The associated-with relationship from motivation.outcome to motivation.constraint is weak; a constrained-by relationship would be more precise.
proposed_change: Replace associated-with toward motivation.constraint with a constrained-by relationship.

subject: motivation.outcome
text: The associated-with relationship between motivation.outcome and motivation.driver is weak; a driver-to-outcome influence relationship would be more precise.
proposed_change: Replace the outcome-to-driver associated-with with a driver --influence--> outcome relationship.

subject: motivation.principle
text: The relationship motivation.principle realizes motivation.goal duplicates the meaning of motivation.principle influence motivation.goal, so two predicates express the same contribution between principle and goal.
proposed_change: Remove the realizes relationship from principle to goal and keep influence.

subject: motivation.principle
text: ArchiMate does not allow a principle to realize a goal, so the relationship motivation.principle realizes motivation.goal conflicts with the standard.
proposed_change: Remove the realizes relationship from principle to goal, or restrict it to cases the standard permits.

subject: motivation.requirement
text: The relationship motivation.requirement --[aggregates]--> motivation.goal inverts the usual hierarchy, since goals are refined by requirements, so it should be removed or reversed.
proposed_change: Remove the requirement aggregates goal relationship or reverse its direction.

subject: motivation.requirement
text: The relationship motivation.requirement --[associated-with]--> motivation.goal overlaps with motivation.requirement --[realizes]--> motivation.goal, and realizes should be preferred when the requirement actually refines the goal.
proposed_change: Prefer realizes over associated-with for requirement-to-goal links where the requirement refines the goal, removing or restricting the associated-with relationship.

subject: motivation.requirement
text: The relationships motivation.requirement --[aggregates]--> motivation.requirement and motivation.requirement --[specializes]--> motivation.requirement must be distinguished as decomposition versus variant.
proposed_change: Define aggregates as decomposition into sub-requirements and specializes as a variant of a requirement, documenting the boundary between them.

subject: motivation.stakeholder
text: The stakeholder associated-with driver and stakeholder influence driver relationships overlap, and influence subsumes association when the stakeholder shapes the driver, so the associated-with variant is redundant unless reserved for passive concern.
proposed_change: Remove stakeholder associated-with driver or restrict it to passive concern, leaving influence for active shaping.

subject: motivation.stakeholder
text: The stakeholder associated-with goal and stakeholder influence goal relationships overlap, and influence subsumes association when the stakeholder shapes the goal, so the associated-with variant is redundant unless reserved for passive concern.
proposed_change: Remove stakeholder associated-with goal or restrict it to passive concern, leaving influence for active shaping.

subject: motivation.stakeholder
text: The stakeholder associated-with constraint relationship is weak, because ArchiMate typically links stakeholders to drivers and goals, with constraints reached via requirements.
proposed_change: Remove stakeholder associated-with constraint and reach constraints through requirements.

subject: motivation.value
text: Apart from value-to-stakeholder, the relationships from motivation.value use generic associated-with, which hides their meaning.
proposed_change: Replace generic associated-with with more specific predicates where a meaningful one exists.

subject: motivation.value
text: The relationship from motivation.value to motivation.outcome would read better as outcome 'delivers' value.
proposed_change: Replace it with a delivers relationship from motivation.outcome to motivation.value.

subject: motivation.value
text: The relationship from motivation.value to motivation.goal would read better as 'supports'.
proposed_change: Change the predicate of the value-to-goal relationship to supports.

subject: motivation.value
text: The relationship from motivation.value to motivation.constraint is weak because constraints restrict the solution, not value.
proposed_change: Remove the value-to-constraint association or reconsider it.

subject: motivation.value
text: The self-association of motivation.value adds little unless it is meant as an aggregation.
proposed_change: Remove the self-association or turn it into an aggregation relationship.

subject: navigation.breadcrumbconfig
text: The relationship navigation.breadcrumbconfig provides navigation.routemeta appears inverted, because RouteMeta normally supplies the breadcrumb label that BreadcrumbConfig consumes.
proposed_change: Reverse the relationship so RouteMeta provides to BreadcrumbConfig, or replace it with a consumes/reads-from relationship from BreadcrumbConfig to RouteMeta.

subject: navigation.breadcrumbconfig
text: The relationship navigation.breadcrumbconfig associated-with navigation.navigationgraph is weak, since the graph's scope implies composition or aggregation.
proposed_change: Replace the weak associated-with relationship with a composition or aggregation relationship (or drop it in favor of the existing navigationgraph aggregates breadcrumbconfig).

subject: navigation.breadcrumbconfig
text: The relationship navigation.breadcrumbconfig tracks navigation.navigationflow borrows an APM predicate for UI progress display, and a predicate like binds-to or renders may fit better.
proposed_change: Change the predicate from tracks to binds-to or renders.

subject: navigation.contextvariable
text: The relationship navigation.contextvariable consumes navigation.route gives agent-like behavior to passive runtime data and its direction is wrong; the route should provide or populate the variable.
proposed_change: Invert it so navigation.route provides or populates navigation.contextvariable, or remove the consumes relationship from contextvariable to route.

subject: navigation.contextvariable
text: The relationship navigation.contextvariable triggers navigation.navigationtransition attributes active behavior to passive data; it would be better modeled as a guard evaluating the variable.
proposed_change: Replace the triggers relationship with a guard (guardcondition or navigationguard) that evaluates the context variable.

subject: navigation.contextvariable
text: The relationship navigation.contextvariable references data-model.jsonschema overlaps with navigation.contextvariable maps-to data-model.schemaproperty when the variable's schema is a property subschema.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: navigation.contextvariable
text: The relationships navigation.contextvariable references application.dataobject and navigation.contextvariable references data-model.jsonschema both describe the value type of the variable and are redundant.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: navigation.flowstep
text: The relationships navigation.flowstep navigates-to navigation.route and navigation.flowstep realizes navigation.route both express the step's binding to one route, so they are redundant.
proposed_change: Keep only one of navigates-to or realizes between FlowStep and Route and remove the other.

subject: navigation.flowstep
text: The relationship navigation.flowstep maps-to ux.view is a data-mapping predicate and duplicates the Route to View rendering relationship.
proposed_change: Remove the maps-to relationship from FlowStep to View.

subject: navigation.flowstep
text: The accesses relationships from navigation.flowstep to data-store.collection, data-model.objectschema and api.operation are indirect because a client-side step does not access them directly.
proposed_change: Remove these direct accesses relationships from FlowStep.

subject: navigation.flowstep
text: The accesses relationship from navigation.flowstep to application.applicationservice largely overlaps with the indirect accesses relationships to Collection, ObjectSchema and Operation.
proposed_change: Reduce the accesses relationships to a single one, or drop the ApplicationService one as overlapping.

subject: navigation.flowstep
text: The relationship navigation.flowstep realizes business.businessfunction is weak because a flow step is ordered while business functions are unordered.
proposed_change: Remove the realizes relationship from FlowStep to BusinessFunction.

subject: navigation.guardaction
text: The depends-on relationship from navigation.guardaction to navigation.guardcondition is indirect, because both attach to a NavigationGuard that evaluates the condition and then invokes the action, so it misrepresents the real dependency.
proposed_change: Remove or replace the direct GuardAction depends-on GuardCondition relationship with guard-level relationships mediated by NavigationGuard.

subject: navigation.guardaction
text: The catalog lacks a Guard-level 'evaluates' relationship from NavigationGuard to GuardCondition and a composes relationship from NavigationGuard to GuardAction, which would express the evaluate-then-invoke flow more accurately.
proposed_change: Add navigationguard evaluates guardcondition and navigationguard composes guardaction relationships.

subject: navigation.guardaction
text: The navigates-to relationship from navigation.guardaction to navigation.route applies only to redirect-type actions, not to block, notify or prompt (cancel, message, confirm) actions.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: navigation.guardcondition
text: The consumes and uses relationships from navigation.guardcondition to navigation.contextvariable express the same meaning (the condition reads flow state), so they are redundant.
proposed_change: Keep only one of the two relationships, preferably consumes or references, and remove the other.

subject: navigation.guardcondition
text: The triggers relationship from navigation.guardcondition to navigation.guardaction is loosely modeled, because the NavigationGuard invokes the guard action on denial and the guard condition itself does not.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: navigation.navigationflow
text: NavigationFlow has both aggregates and composes relationships to FlowStep, which conflict; since a FlowStep exists only within its flow, composes is correct.
proposed_change: Drop the aggregates relationship from navigation.navigationflow to navigation.flowstep and keep composes.

subject: navigation.navigationflow
text: The realizes relationship from NavigationFlow to motivation.goal is questionable, since supports fits better than realizing a goal.
proposed_change: Replace realizes with supports for the NavigationFlow to Goal relationship.

subject: navigation.navigationflow
text: The accesses relationship from NavigationFlow to ux.view overlaps the existing step-to-route-to-view chain.
proposed_change: Remove the direct accesses relationship to ux.view and rely on the step-to-route-to-view chain.

subject: navigation.navigationflow
text: The flows-to predicate from NavigationFlow to NavigationTransition is odd, since a flow traverses or references transitions.
proposed_change: Change the predicate from flows-to to traverses or references.

subject: navigation.navigationflow
text: The uses relationship from NavigationFlow to technology.systemsoftware is weakly meaningful for a client-side flow.
proposed_change: Remove the uses relationship to technology.systemsoftware.

subject: navigation.navigationgraph
text: navigation.navigationgraph has both aggregates and composes relationships to navigation.route, which gives contradictory lifecycle semantics for the same pair.
proposed_change: Keep only the composes relationship from navigationgraph to route and remove the aggregates relationship.

subject: navigation.navigationgraph
text: navigation.navigationgraph has both aggregates and composes relationships to navigation.navigationtransition, which gives contradictory lifecycle semantics for the same pair.
proposed_change: Keep only the composes relationship from navigationgraph to navigationtransition and remove the aggregates relationship.

subject: navigation.navigationgraph
text: The uses relationship from navigation.navigationgraph to technology.systemsoftware is weak, because a front-end route table depends mainly on a router library or the browser rather than on host system software.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: navigation.navigationguard
text: The relationships navigation.navigationguard evaluates guardcondition and navigation.navigationguard uses guardcondition are redundant; evaluates is the more precise one.
proposed_change: Remove the uses relationship to guardcondition and keep evaluates.

subject: navigation.navigationguard
text: The accesses relationship from navigation.navigationguard to data-store.collection is odd for client-side guard code unless the store is browser-local.
proposed_change: Remove it or restrict it to browser-local stores.

subject: navigation.navigationguard
text: The implements relationship from navigation.navigationguard to security.securitypolicy overstates what a client-side guard does; enforces fits better, and real enforcement belongs on the server.
proposed_change: Replace implements with enforces.

subject: navigation.navigationguard
text: The requires relationship from navigation.navigationguard to security.role overlaps with the references relationship to business.businessrole.
proposed_change: Clarify the boundary between the two role relationships or merge them.

subject: navigation.navigationguard
text: The uses relationship from navigation.navigationguard to technology.systemsoftware stretches the target type, since router libraries are not system software.
proposed_change: Remove the relationship or retarget it to a more fitting type.

subject: navigation.navigationtransition
text: The relationships navigation.navigationtransition flows-to navigation.route and navigation.navigationtransition navigates-to navigation.route are redundant because both express the transition's destination route.
proposed_change: Keep navigates-to (the UX-specific predicate) and remove flows-to from navigationtransition to route.

subject: navigation.navigationtransition
text: The relationship navigation.navigationtransition triggers navigation.guardaction is indirect, since the guard triggers its action on denial and the transition only causes it through requires NavigationGuard.
proposed_change: Remove the direct triggers relationship from navigationtransition to guardaction, relying on requires NavigationGuard instead.

subject: navigation.route
text: The relationships navigation.route associated-with navigation.routemeta and navigation.route composes navigation.routemeta express the same meaning and are redundant.
proposed_change: Remove associated-with and keep composes between navigation.route and navigation.routemeta.

subject: navigation.route
text: The relationships navigation.route flows-to navigation.navigationtransition and navigation.route triggers navigation.navigationtransition overlap in meaning.
proposed_change: Consolidate flows-to and triggers into a single relationship between route and navigationtransition.

subject: navigation.route
text: The relationships navigation.route uses application.applicationservice and navigation.route resolves-with application.applicationservice overlap in meaning.
proposed_change: Consolidate uses and resolves-with into one relationship between route and applicationservice.

subject: navigation.route
text: Direct relationships from the client route navigation.route to data-store elements (Collection, View, AccessPattern) bypass the API layer and look dubious.
proposed_change: Remove or reconsider direct route-to-data-store relationships so access goes through the API layer.

subject: navigation.route
text: The relationship navigation.route realizes motivation.outcome uses a predicate that does not fit; supports-goals or delivers-value would be more appropriate.
proposed_change: Replace realizes with supports-goals or delivers-value.

subject: navigation.route
text: The relationship navigation.route uses ux.layoutconfig is attached to the wrong source, since LayoutConfig is normally applied to the View rather than the Route.
proposed_change: Move the layoutconfig relationship to ux.view instead of navigation.route.

subject: navigation.routemeta
text: The 'serves' relationship from navigation.routemeta to navigation.route is weak because route metadata is part of the route, so composition (Route composes RouteMeta) fits better; this duplicates the existing route-composes-routemeta relationship.
proposed_change: Remove the routemeta serves route relationship and rely on navigation.route composes navigation.routemeta.

subject: navigation.routemeta
text: The 'uses' relationship from navigation.routemeta to navigation.navigationtransition conflates the visual animation named in the meta 'transition' field with the NavigationTransition element, which is a route-change edge.
proposed_change: Remove or rework the uses relationship to navigation.navigationtransition so it no longer equates the animation name with the route-change edge element.

subject: navigation.routemeta
text: The 'governs' relationship from navigation.routemeta to navigation.navigationguard overstates the role of route metadata, which only supplies hints while the guard does the governing.
proposed_change: Change the predicate from 'governs' to 'references'.

subject: product.capability
text: The relationship product.capability --[fulfills]--> motivation.requirement partially overlaps with the traceability predicate satisfies/fulfills-requirements, so a single convention for linking to requirements should be chosen.
proposed_change: Choose one predicate convention (fulfills or satisfies) for capability-to-requirement traceability and remove or align the other.

subject: product.capability
text: The product.capability --[aggregates]--> product.capability relationship could be confused with composes; aggregation is only appropriate if sub-capabilities can be shared or regrouped.
proposed_change: Clarify that aggregates applies only when sub-capabilities can be shared or regrouped, and use composes otherwise.

subject: product.feature
text: The product.feature delivers-value relationship to motivation.value overlaps with delivers/supports relationships from the motivation layer, which the note considers acceptable.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: product.feature
text: The product.feature uses relationship to product.capability risks being confused with the realizes relationship to the same capability, so a feature should not both realize and use the same capability.
proposed_change: Add an editor/validation rule that a feature must not both realize and use the same capability.

subject: product.feature
text: The cross-layer product.feature realizes business.businessservice relationship may be redundant because application services usually realize business services, so the link is already implied via capability.
proposed_change: Consider removing the feature realizes businessservice relationship or relying on the path via capability.

subject: product.persona
text: The relationship 'product.persona serves business.businessrole' is semantically wrong because a persona does not provide service to a role; it describes the people who fill the role.
proposed_change: Replace the 'serves' predicate with 'associated-with' or 'references'.

subject: product.persona
text: The relationship 'product.persona realizes motivation.stakeholder' is questionable because a fictional archetype does not implement a stakeholder.
proposed_change: Replace 'realizes' with 'associated-with' or introduce a dedicated 'represents' predicate.

subject: product.userworkflow
text: The relationship product.userworkflow composes product.feature is semantically wrong because features exist independently of any workflow and are shared across journeys.
proposed_change: Replace composes with aggregates or uses for the userworkflow-to-feature relationship.

subject: product.userworkflow
text: The relationship product.userworkflow aggregates business.businessprocess looks inverted; a user journey more naturally supports or realizes part of a business process.
proposed_change: Replace aggregates with supports or realizes, with the workflow supporting or realizing the business process.

subject: product.userworkflow
text: The relationship product.userworkflow uses product.capability is largely derivable via workflow steps to features to capabilities, so it is partly redundant.
proposed_change: Consider removing the direct uses relationship to capability since it is derivable through steps and features.

subject: product.workflowstep
text: The relationships product.workflowstep uses product.capability and product.workflowstep uses product.feature overlap, because features realise capabilities and the step-to-capability link can be derived via step-to-feature-to-capability.
proposed_change: Keep the workflowstep-uses-capability relationship only for steps whose feature is not yet defined, treating it otherwise as derived from the feature link.

subject: product.workflowstep
text: The relationship product.workflowstep serves product.persona uses a loose predicate, since the persona performs the step; 'performed-by' would read more naturally.
proposed_change: Replace 'serves' with a 'performed-by' predicate for the workflowstep-to-persona relationship.

subject: security.accesscondition
text: The relationship security.accesscondition composes security.policyrule has an inverted direction: the part (AccessCondition) composes the whole (PolicyRule), contrary to the catalog convention that the whole composes the part.
proposed_change: Swap the direction so PolicyRule composes AccessCondition, or use a 'composed-of' predicate.

subject: security.accesscondition
text: The relationship security.accesscondition uses security.validationrule muddles concerns, since validation rules accept or reject data values while access conditions make access decisions.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: security.accesscondition
text: The relationship security.accesscondition governs security.fieldaccesscontrol partly overlaps in meaning with the constrains relationship.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: security.accountabilityrequirement
text: The three 'requires' relationships from security.accountabilityrequirement to AuditConfig, Evidence and RetentionPolicy partly overlap, because Evidence such as audit trails is produced by AuditConfig and kept under RetentionPolicy.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: security.accountabilityrequirement
text: The 'constrains' relationship from security.accountabilityrequirement to security.actor is loosely used, because the obligation restricts how the actor may act rather than limiting the actor itself.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: security.actor
text: Actor has both associated-with and references relationships to Delegation, which are near-redundant; one should be kept, ideally with explicit delegator/delegatee roles.
proposed_change: Keep one relationship between Actor and Delegation and make delegator/delegatee roles explicit.

subject: security.actor
text: Actor has both governed-by and requires relationships to AuthenticationConfig, which overlap heavily.
proposed_change: Collapse governed-by and requires into a single relationship between Actor and AuthenticationConfig.

subject: security.actor
text: The Actor associated-with Threat relationship conflicts with the Threat definition, which excludes the principal who carries out the attack.
proposed_change: Remove the Actor associated-with Threat relationship or revise the Threat definition to allow threat actors.

subject: security.auditconfig
text: The relationships security.auditconfig depends-on security.retentionpolicy and security.auditconfig governs security.retentionpolicy point in opposite directions relative to security.retentionpolicy governs security.auditconfig, and governs contradicts the scope statement that retention belongs to RetentionPolicy.
proposed_change: Remove the governs relationship from security.auditconfig to security.retentionpolicy.

subject: security.auditconfig
text: The relationships security.auditconfig governs security.secureresource and security.auditconfig monitors security.secureresource overlap in meaning, and monitors fits better.
proposed_change: Drop governs to security.secureresource and keep monitors.

subject: security.auditconfig
text: The predicate triggers from security.auditconfig to security.evidence would read better as generates, since the config emits the artifact.
proposed_change: Replace the triggers predicate with generates for auditconfig to evidence.

subject: security.authenticationconfig
text: The references and uses relationships from security.authenticationconfig to security.passwordpolicy are redundant, since an authentication config that names its credential policy also applies it, so uses subsumes references.
proposed_change: Keep only the uses relationship and remove the references relationship from security.authenticationconfig to security.passwordpolicy.

subject: security.authenticationconfig
text: The depends-on relationship from security.authenticationconfig to security.auditconfig is questionable because authentication usually emits events to audit rather than requiring audit in order to function.
proposed_change: Replace or remove depends-on to auditconfig in favor of a predicate expressing that authentication emits events to audit (e.g., reporting to audit).

subject: security.bindingofduty
text: The constrains relationship (bindingofduty to role) and the governs relationship (bindingofduty to resourceoperation) both express the rule restricting access through the influence family, differing only in target, and could be unified.
proposed_change: Unify the constrains and governs relationships into a single relationship type.

subject: security.bindingofduty
text: The requires relationship from bindingofduty to evidence is labelled ArchiMate Access, but for Evidence it is better read as a data dependency.
proposed_change: Relabel the requires predicate mapping from ArchiMate Access to a data dependency reading.

subject: security.bindingofduty
text: Binding of duty and separation of duty are complementary and should be modelled as such rather than merely 'associated-with'.
proposed_change: Replace the generic associated-with predicate between them with a predicate expressing complementarity.

subject: security.condition
text: The 'composes' relationship from security.condition to security.accesscondition may be too strong, because AccessConditions are also evaluated on their own within PolicyRules, ResourceOperations and InformationRights and so exist independently of a Condition; 'aggregates' would fit better.
proposed_change: Change the predicate of security.condition -> security.accesscondition from 'composes' to 'aggregates'.

subject: security.condition
text: The 'triggers' relationship from security.condition to security.policyaction partly duplicates PolicyRule obligation triggering and bypasses the permit/deny decision step.
proposed_change: Remove or rework the condition triggers policyaction relationship so that actions are triggered through PolicyRule obligations after the permit/deny decision.

subject: security.countermeasure
text: The relationship security.countermeasure implements security.securitypolicy points the wrong way: concrete configuration implements countermeasures, not the reverse.
proposed_change: Remove or reverse the implements relationship so that the policy or configuration implements the countermeasure.

subject: security.countermeasure
text: The relationship security.countermeasure realizes motivation.goal is too strong for a qualitative goal; supports fits better.
proposed_change: Replace the realizes predicate with supports.

subject: security.countermeasure
text: The relationship security.countermeasure fulfills security.securityconstraints overlaps with security.countermeasure satisfies motivation.requirement.
proposed_change: Remove one of the two overlapping relationships or clearly distinguish their semantics.

subject: security.countermeasure
text: The relationships security.countermeasure monitors security.secureresource and security.countermeasure protects security.secureresource overlap; monitors suits only detective controls.
proposed_change: Merge into protects, or restrict monitors to detective controls and document the distinction.

subject: security.dataclassification
text: The governs relationships from security.dataclassification to security.secureresource and security.fieldaccesscontrol overlap with the label-to-asset relationship already held by security.informationentity, since classification applies to resources only indirectly through information entities.
proposed_change: Remove the governs relationships to secureresource and fieldaccesscontrol and rely on the informationentity relationship for indirect application to resources.

subject: security.dataclassification
text: The requires relationship from security.dataclassification to security.countermeasure duplicates the governance notion of 'mandates', which fits better because a classification label does not need a control in order to function.
proposed_change: Replace the 'requires' predicate with 'mandates' for the relationship from dataclassification to countermeasure.

subject: security.delegation
text: The relationship security.delegation requires security.actor merges two distinct roles, delegator and delegatee, into a single edge so the roles cannot be told apart.
proposed_change: Replace the single requires edge with separate role-specific relationships (delegator and delegatee) or add role-qualified attributes.

subject: security.delegation
text: The relationship security.delegation authorizes security.role covers only delegation of roles, not delegation of individual permissions, although the delegation definition allows permission delegation.
proposed_change: Add a relationship from security.delegation to security.permission (e.g. authorizes) so individual permissions can be delegated.

subject: security.evidence
text: The relationship security.evidence --[realizes]--> security.auditconfig is inverted in spirit: evidence is the output of AuditConfig, so a 'generated-by' style predicate fits better than realization.
proposed_change: Replace 'realizes' with a generated-by relationship (e.g. auditconfig triggers/generates evidence) or reverse its direction.

subject: security.evidence
text: The relationship security.evidence --[validates]--> security.policyrule uses a predicate that belongs to the testing category and fits evidence poorly.
proposed_change: Replace 'validates' with 'references' or 'supports'.

subject: security.evidence
text: The relationship security.evidence --[mitigates]--> security.threat is too broad because evidence is detective rather than preventive, so it applies only to repudiation-type threats.
proposed_change: Restrict or qualify 'mitigates' to repudiation-type threats, or replace the predicate.

subject: security.fieldaccesscontrol
text: The relationships security.fieldaccesscontrol governs security.secureresource and security.fieldaccesscontrol protects security.secureresource overlap, since both describe the field rule acting on the resource's field.
proposed_change: Keep only the protects relationship and remove governs from security.fieldaccesscontrol to security.secureresource.

subject: security.fieldaccesscontrol
text: SecureResource is described as owning its FieldAccessControls, so the governs relationship from FieldAccessControl to SecureResource has the wrong direction and predicate; a composition from the resource side would be more accurate.
proposed_change: Replace governs with a composes relationship from security.secureresource to security.fieldaccesscontrol.

subject: security.informationentity
text: The relationship security.informationentity --[governs]--> security.informationright points the wrong way, because the right grants access to the entity; a predicate such as 'referenced-by' or 'governed-by' would fit better.
proposed_change: Reverse the relationship or replace 'governs' with 'referenced-by' or 'governed-by'.

subject: security.informationentity
text: The relationship security.informationentity --[constrained-by]--> security.retentionpolicy may stretch the definition of retention policy, since retention policy is scoped to security-relevant data such as audit logs and keys, not general information categories like PII.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: security.informationright
text: The relationship security.informationright --[governs]--> security.informationentity largely duplicates security.informationright --[accesses]--> security.informationentity, since both state that the right targets one information category.
proposed_change: Remove one of the two relationships, most likely the 'governs' relationship, and keep 'accesses'.

subject: security.informationright
text: The relationship security.informationright --[implements]--> security.permission is questionable because InformationRight is defined as distinct from a role-assigned Permission, so 'implements' does not fit; 'realizes' or 'references' may fit better.
proposed_change: Replace the 'implements' predicate with 'realizes' or 'references' for the relationship to security.permission.

subject: security.needtoknow
text: The relationships security.needtoknow constrains security.permission and security.needtoknow implements security.policyrule overlap: if the need-to-know constraint is realized as a policy rule, the rule rather than the constraint is what restricts the permission.
proposed_change: Remove or reconcile one of the two relationships so that either the constraint or the policy rule is the element that restricts the permission.

subject: security.needtoknow
text: The relationship security.needtoknow associated-with security.role uses a vague predicate; a more specific predicate such as constrains would better express that need-to-know narrows role-based access.
proposed_change: Replace the associated-with predicate with a more specific one such as constrains.

subject: security.passwordpolicy
text: The mandates and requires relationships from security.passwordpolicy to security.countermeasure overlap; since Countermeasure is defined as implemented or mandated by configuration types, requires is redundant or ambiguous.
proposed_change: Remove the requires relationship from PasswordPolicy to Countermeasure and keep mandates.

subject: security.passwordpolicy
text: The mitigates relationship from security.passwordpolicy to security.threat partly duplicates the path PasswordPolicy to Countermeasure to Threat.
proposed_change: Remove or reconsider the direct mitigates relationship to Threat in favor of the path via Countermeasure.

subject: security.passwordpolicy
text: The constrains relationship from security.passwordpolicy to security.authenticationconfig may have the wrong direction and would be better expressed as AuthenticationConfig referencing or using PasswordPolicy.
proposed_change: Drop the constrains relationship and rely on authenticationconfig references/uses passwordpolicy.

subject: security.policyaction
text: The relationships security.policyaction mandates security.countermeasure and security.policyaction requires security.countermeasure overlap heavily in meaning, so only one should be kept.
proposed_change: Keep one of mandates or requires toward Countermeasure and remove the other.

subject: security.policyaction
text: The relationship security.policyaction governs security.permission is questionable because a PolicyAction is an obligation executed after a decision, not a rule-giver over grants.
proposed_change: Remove or rethink the governs relationship from PolicyAction to Permission.

subject: security.policyaction
text: The relationship security.policyaction enforces-requirement security.policyrule inverts the usual model in which the rule contains or triggers the action.
proposed_change: Replace it with a composed-of or triggered-by relationship oriented between PolicyRule and PolicyAction.

subject: security.policyaction
text: The relationship security.policyaction mitigates security.threat partially duplicates the path through Countermeasure.
proposed_change: Remove the direct mitigates relationship to Threat or consolidate it with the Countermeasure path.

subject: security.policyrule
text: The relationships security.policyrule mandates security.countermeasure and security.policyrule requires security.countermeasure overlap in meaning.
proposed_change: Keep only the mandates relationship and remove requires.

subject: security.policyrule
text: The relationships security.policyrule uses security.accesscondition and security.policyrule uses security.condition are partly redundant because a Condition may itself compose AccessConditions.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: security.policyrule
text: The 'composes' relationship from security.policyrule to security.securitypolicy reads ambiguously, so its direction as part-of-whole needs confirmation.
proposed_change: Confirm the direction is part-of-whole (PolicyRule is part of SecurityPolicy) and clarify the predicate semantics.

subject: security.policyrule
text: The relationship security.policyrule governs security.informationright is questionable because InformationRight carries its own condition and is arguably independent of PolicyRule.
proposed_change: Reconsider or remove the governs relationship to InformationRight.

subject: security.resourceoperation
text: The accesses and governs relationships from security.resourceoperation to security.secureresource overlap in meaning between the same pair of types.
proposed_change: Collapse accesses and governs into a single relationship between ResourceOperation and SecureResource.

subject: security.resourceoperation
text: The definition says the resource owns its operations, which suggests SecureResource composes ResourceOperation, whereas the catalog currently uses aggregates from secureresource to resourceoperation.
proposed_change: Change the secureresource-to-resourceoperation relationship from aggregates to composes.

subject: security.resourceoperation
text: The governs relationship from security.resourceoperation to security.secureresource is only weakly justified, via rate limits and conditions.
proposed_change: Remove the governs relationship from ResourceOperation to SecureResource.

subject: security.resourceoperation
text: The triggers relationship from security.resourceoperation to security.auditconfig is semantically loose, since an operation triggers audit events rather than the configuration.
proposed_change: Replace the triggers predicate with uses or references.

subject: security.retentionpolicy
text: The relationships security.retentionpolicy mandates security.countermeasure and security.retentionpolicy requires security.countermeasure overlap heavily, since both say the policy needs a control.
proposed_change: Keep mandates for the normative obligation and drop requires, or redefine requires strictly as an operational dependency.

subject: security.retentionpolicy
text: The relationships security.retentionpolicy constrains security.informationentity and security.retentionpolicy governs security.evidence express similar lifecycle control.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: security.role
text: The relationships aggregates, authorizes and provides from security.role to security.permission all express the same role-grants-permission membership, so only aggregates is needed.
proposed_change: Keep security.role aggregates security.permission and remove the authorizes and provides relationships to security.permission.

subject: security.role
text: The relationship security.role accesses security.secureresource is derivable via Permission and is therefore redundant.
proposed_change: Remove the accesses relationship from security.role to security.secureresource.

subject: security.role
text: The relationship security.role specializes security.role correctly models single-parent inheritance but should be restricted to one parent.
proposed_change: Restrict the specializes relationship from security.role to security.role to a single parent (cardinality at most one).

subject: security.secureresource
text: The aggregates relationship from security.secureresource to security.fieldaccesscontrol is semantically weak because a FieldAccessControl is bound to one field of a single resource and cannot exist without it, so composes fits the lifecycle dependency better.
proposed_change: Change the predicate of secureresource -> fieldaccesscontrol from aggregates to composes.

subject: security.secureresource
text: The aggregates relationship from security.secureresource to security.resourceoperation is semantically weak because a ResourceOperation is declared on a single resource and cannot exist without it, so composes fits the lifecycle dependency better.
proposed_change: Change the predicate of secureresource -> resourceoperation from aggregates to composes.

subject: security.securityconstraints
text: The enforces and governs relationships from security.securityconstraints to security.securitypolicy express overlapping meaning.
proposed_change: Keep only the governs relationship and remove enforces.

subject: security.securityconstraints
text: The enforces and governs relationships from security.securityconstraints to security.securitypolicy conflict with the definition of SecurityConstraints as a container with no decision logic.
proposed_change: Remove these links from the container or move them onto the individual duty rules (SeparationOfDuty, BindingOfDuty, NeedToKnow).

subject: security.securityconstraints
text: The constrains relationship from security.securityconstraints to security.role conflicts with the container definition, because constraints on roles come from the aggregated rules rather than from the container itself.
proposed_change: Move the role-constraining link onto the individual duty rules or remove it from the container.

subject: security.securityconstraints
text: The implements relationship from security.securityconstraints to motivation.constraint would read more naturally as realizes.
proposed_change: Replace implements with realizes.

subject: security.securitymodel
text: SecurityModel links to AuthenticationConfig with both aggregates and composes, which is contradictory; only composes should remain since there is one config per application.
proposed_change: Remove the aggregates relationship from SecurityModel to AuthenticationConfig and keep composes.

subject: security.securitymodel
text: SecurityModel has both composes and governs relationships to SecurityPolicy, and governs is redundant with containment.
proposed_change: Remove the governs relationship from SecurityModel to SecurityPolicy.

subject: security.securitymodel
text: SecurityModel has both aggregates and manages relationships to Threat, which overlap in meaning.
proposed_change: Collapse the two into a single relationship, dropping one of aggregates or manages.

subject: security.securitymodel
text: The constrains relationship from SecurityModel to AccountabilityRequirement has weak semantics because a container does not restrict its members; aggregates would fit better.
proposed_change: Replace constrains with aggregates for SecurityModel to AccountabilityRequirement.

subject: security.securitypolicy
text: The relationships security.securitypolicy mandates Countermeasure and security.securitypolicy requires Countermeasure largely overlap in meaning.
proposed_change: Keep one of mandates/requires or sharpen the distinction between them.

subject: security.securitypolicy
text: The relationship security.securitypolicy aggregates PolicyRule should arguably be composes, since rules do not exist outside their policy.
proposed_change: Change the aggregates predicate to composes.

subject: security.securitypolicy
text: The relationship security.securitypolicy enforces-requirement AccessCondition is odd because conditions are evaluated within rules, not requirements.
proposed_change: Replace with a composed-of relationship via PolicyRule or an evaluates relationship.

subject: security.securitypolicy
text: The relationships security.securitypolicy realizes Principle and security.securitypolicy satisfies Requirement may overlap.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: security.separationofduty
text: The relationships security.separationofduty constrains business.businessrole and security.separationofduty constrains security.role express the same role-exclusion at different layers, and are likely redundant if security roles map one-to-one to business roles.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: security.separationofduty
text: The associated-with relationship from security.separationofduty to security.bindingofduty is vague, and a more specific predicate should be reviewed even though none is currently available.
proposed_change: Review replacing associated-with with a more specific predicate if one becomes available.

subject: security.threat
text: The relationship security.threat accesses security.secureresource duplicates security.threat targets security.secureresource, so the two express the same meaning.
proposed_change: Remove the accesses relationship and keep targets.

subject: security.threat
text: The relationship security.threat aggregates security.countermeasure inverts the natural 'countermeasure mitigates threat' direction and is not a whole-part relationship.
proposed_change: Remove the aggregates relationship and rely on security.countermeasure mitigates security.threat.

subject: security.threat
text: The relationship security.threat maps-to motivation.requirement uses maps-to, a data-schema predicate, for traceability, which misfits its semantics.
proposed_change: Replace maps-to with a traceability-appropriate predicate such as influence or associated-with.

subject: security.threat
text: The relationship security.threat realizes motivation.driver is semantically wrong because a threat does not realize a driver.
proposed_change: Replace realizes with influence or associated-with.

subject: security.threat
text: The relationships security.threat triggers security.auditconfig and security.threat constrains security.accesscondition describe design motivation rather than runtime triggering or constraint.
proposed_change: Replace triggers and constrains with influence.

subject: security.validationrule
text: The relationships security.validationrule constrains security.fieldaccesscontrol and security.validationrule enforces-requirement security.fieldaccesscontrol largely overlap, so only one should be kept.
proposed_change: Keep one of the two relationships from ValidationRule to FieldAccessControl and remove the other.

subject: security.validationrule
text: The relationship security.validationrule realizes security.policyrule is doubtful because validation rules accept or reject values and do not decide access, whereas PolicyRule yields access decisions.
proposed_change: Remove the realizes relationship from ValidationRule to PolicyRule.

subject: security.validationrule
text: The relationship security.validationrule enforces-requirement security.securityconstraints is a weak fit because SecurityConstraints are procedural duty rules and ValidationRule is a value-validation construct.
proposed_change: Remove the enforces-requirement relationship from ValidationRule to SecurityConstraints.

subject: security.validationrule
text: The relationship security.validationrule constrains security.accesscondition is a weak fit for a value-validation construct.
proposed_change: Remove the constrains relationship from ValidationRule to AccessCondition.

subject: technology.artifact
text: The artifact-to-artifact relationships aggregates and composes are easy to confuse, and the spec gives no clear rule (such as independent publishability) for choosing between them.
proposed_change: Document a selection rule, such as independent publishability, that distinguishes aggregates from composes between artifacts.

subject: technology.artifact
text: The relationship technology.artifact realizes technology.technologyservice is semantically weak because in ArchiMate artifacts normally realize application components or data objects, while services are realized by node or system-software behavior.
proposed_change: Remove or rework the artifact realizes technologyservice relationship, so that services are realized by node or systemsoftware behavior instead.

subject: technology.communicationnetwork
text: The relationships technology.communicationnetwork connects technology.node and technology.communicationnetwork serves technology.node largely overlap in meaning, so only one should be kept.
proposed_change: Keep only one of the connects or serves relationships from communicationnetwork to node.

subject: technology.communicationnetwork
text: The assigned-to relationship from technology.communicationnetwork to technology.technologycollaboration misuses Assignment, which is meant for active-structure-to-behavior/role, because a collaboration is itself active structure.
proposed_change: Replace assigned-to with aggregation or association for communicationnetwork to technologycollaboration.

subject: technology.communicationnetwork
text: The provides relationship from technology.communicationnetwork to technology.technologyinterface conflicts with the interface definition, which says interfaces are located on nodes, devices or system software.
proposed_change: Remove or rework the provides relationship to technologyinterface.

subject: technology.communicationnetwork
text: The associated-with relationship from technology.communicationnetwork to technology.systemsoftware is too vague to be useful.
proposed_change: Remove the associated-with relationship or replace it with a more specific one.

subject: technology.device
text: The relationship technology.device composes technology.systemsoftware is questionable because system software is installed on hardware rather than being a structural part of it; ArchiMate would use assignment or a hosts notion.
proposed_change: Replace the composes relationship with an assignment or hosts-style relationship between device and systemsoftware.

subject: technology.device
text: The relationship technology.device satisfies security.securitypolicy is odd because an access-control policy is evaluated rather than satisfied by hardware; constrained-by or governed-by fits better.
proposed_change: Change the predicate from satisfies to constrained-by or governed-by.

subject: technology.device
text: The relationship technology.device serves application.applicationcomponent bypasses technology.node, which would be the intermediate hosting element.
proposed_change: Route the relationship through technology.node, removing or replacing the direct device-to-applicationcomponent serves.

subject: technology.node
text: The relationship 'technology.node serves business.businessprocess' skips the application layer and would be better expressed through ApplicationComponent or TechnologyService.
proposed_change: Remove the direct Node serves BusinessProcess relationship and express it via application.applicationcomponent or technology.technologyservice.

subject: technology.node
text: The relationship 'technology.node composes technology.artifact' overlaps with deployment semantics, since artifacts are typically assigned or deployed to a node rather than composed by it.
proposed_change: Replace composes with an assigned-to/deployed relationship between node and artifact.

subject: technology.node
text: The relationship 'technology.node satisfies security.securitypolicy' is questionable because policies are enforced by policy enforcement points, so 'enforces' or 'governed-by' may fit better than 'satisfies'.
proposed_change: Change the predicate from satisfies to enforces or governed-by.

subject: technology.path
text: The relationships technology.path flows-to technology.technologyservice and technology.path realizes technology.technologyservice overlap ambiguously in meaning.
proposed_change: Clarify or consolidate the two relationships so that only one expresses path-to-service traffic, keeping realizes only for connectivity services.

subject: technology.systemsoftware
text: The relationship technology.systemsoftware composes technology.artifact is questionable because in ArchiMate artifacts realize system software, and it overlaps with the accesses relationship to artifact.
proposed_change: Remove or reverse the composes relationship to artifact (artifact realizes system software) and clarify its boundary with accesses.

subject: technology.systemsoftware
text: The relationship technology.systemsoftware realizes business.businessservice skips the intermediate layers.
proposed_change: Remove the direct realizes relationship to business service, or route it via application or technology service.

subject: technology.systemsoftware
text: The relationship technology.systemsoftware realizes motivation.goal skips layers and supports would suit a goal better.
proposed_change: Replace realizes with supports for the relationship to goal.

subject: technology.systemsoftware
text: The relationship technology.systemsoftware implements motivation.principle likely should be a governed-by-principles relationship.
proposed_change: Replace implements with governed-by-principles for the relationship to principle.

subject: technology.systemsoftware
text: The relationships serves and assigned-to from technology.systemsoftware to technology.technologyfunction may confuse modelers about which to use.
proposed_change: Clarify the distinction between serves and assigned-to, or keep only one of them.

subject: technology.systemsoftware
text: The relationships implements security.countermeasure and mitigates security.threat from technology.systemsoftware largely duplicate each other.
proposed_change: Consolidate into one of the two relationships.

subject: technology.technologycollaboration
text: The two 'uses' relationships from technology.technologycollaboration to communicationnetwork and to path partially overlap, since a path normally runs over a network, so modelling both from the collaboration may be redundant.
proposed_change: Remove one of the two 'uses' relationships or define a rule for when each is used.

subject: technology.technologycollaboration
text: The aggregates relationship from technology.technologycollaboration to technology.technologyinterface is unusual because interfaces normally compose a single active element, so the collaboration-level endpoint should be the explicit target.
proposed_change: Replace the aggregation of technologyinterface with an explicit collaboration-level interface endpoint as target, or drop the aggregation.

subject: technology.technologyevent
text: The flows-to relationship from technology.technologyevent to technology.artifact is questionable because ArchiMate Flow links behavior elements, and an event writing to a passive artifact should be an Access (accesses/writes) relationship.
proposed_change: Replace the flows-to relationship from technologyevent to artifact with an accesses/writes relationship.

subject: technology.technologyevent
text: The flows-to and triggers relationships from technology.technologyevent to technology.technologyprocess overlap in meaning, since triggering usually implies the payload is handed over, so modelers cannot easily choose between them unless the spec states when each applies.
proposed_change: Remove one of the two relationships or document in the spec when flows-to versus triggers applies between technologyevent and technologyprocess.

subject: technology.technologyfunction
text: The relationship technology.technologyfunction triggers technology.technologyprocess partly overlaps with technology.technologyfunction flows-to technology.technologyprocess, so modelers may encode the same connection twice.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: technology.technologyfunction
text: The direct triggers relationship from technology.technologyfunction to technology.technologyprocess overlaps with the indirect path through technology.technologyevent (function triggers event, event triggers process), so modelers may double-encode the same triggering.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: technology.technologyfunction
text: The relationship technology.technologyfunction serves business.businessservice skips the usual technology-service/application layering and may be better expressed by the function realizing a technology.technologyservice that serves the business layer.
proposed_change: Remove or discourage the direct serves relationship to business.businessservice and express it via realizes technology.technologyservice, which then serves the business layer.

subject: technology.technologyinteraction
text: The relationship technologyinteraction realizes technologycollaboration is semantically wrong because behavior does not realize active structure; in ArchiMate the collaboration is assigned to the interaction.
proposed_change: Remove the realizes relationship to technologycollaboration and rely on the collaboration-to-interaction assignment (the existing performs relationship, as the inverse of assigned-to).

subject: technology.technologyinteraction
text: The relationship technologyinteraction composes technologyfunction is questionable because a function is performed by a single node, so a multi-participant interaction being part of a function conflicts with both definitions.
proposed_change: Replace composes with aggregation or flow-to between technologyinteraction and technologyfunction.

subject: technology.technologyinterface
text: The relationships technologyinterface assigned-to node and technologyinterface assigned-to systemsoftware invert the ArchiMate convention, in which nodes and system software are composed of or assigned their interfaces.
proposed_change: Replace the interface-to-node and interface-to-systemsoftware assigned-to relationships with composed-of (node/systemsoftware composes interface), or reverse their direction.

subject: technology.technologyinterface
text: The relationship technologyinterface assigned-to technologyservice matches the ArchiMate convention.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: technology.technologyinterface
text: The 'uses' relationships from technologyinterface to communicationnetwork and to path duplicate ArchiMate Association/Realization semantics and do not fit.
proposed_change: Remove or replace the 'uses' relationships toward communicationnetwork and path with the appropriate ArchiMate relationship (association or realization).

subject: technology.technologyinterface
text: The two 'uses' relationships from technologyinterface (to communicationnetwork and to path) overlap when a path is realized by a network.
proposed_change: Consolidate the two 'uses' relationships into one or remove one of them.

subject: technology.technologyservice
text: The relationships technology.technologyservice realizes business.businessservice and technology.technologyservice serves business.businessservice overlap in meaning, and realizing a business service directly from a technology service is unusual.
proposed_change: Remove or restrict the realizes relationship to business.businessservice and keep serves.

subject: technology.technologyservice
text: The relationships technology.technologyservice provides technology.technologyinterface and technology.technologyservice serves technology.technologyinterface are inverted, since interfaces normally serve or are assigned to services.
proposed_change: Remove or invert these relationships so the interface serves or is assigned to the technology service (an assigned-to relationship already exists).

subject: technology.technologyservice
text: The relationships technology.technologyservice aggregates technology.technologyfunction and technology.technologyservice aggregates technology.technologyprocess invert ArchiMate, where functions and processes realize services.
proposed_change: Remove the aggregates relationships and rely on technologyfunction and technologyprocess realizes technologyservice.

subject: technology.technologyservice
text: The relationship technology.technologyservice consumes technology.artifact uses a predicate that suits active use, but an artifact is passive, so accesses fits better.
proposed_change: Replace consumes with accesses for the relationship to technology.artifact.

subject: technology.technologyservice
text: The relationships technology.technologyservice realizes motivation.goal and technology.technologyservice serves motivation.stakeholder are weak links; requirement or outcome targets are preferable.
proposed_change: Replace these with relationships to motivation.requirement or motivation outcome.

subject: testing.contextvariation
text: The 'serves' relationship from testing.contextvariation to testing.testcoveragetarget uses a predicate that does not fit, because a context variation does not provide a service to the target but qualifies the conditions under which the target is tested.
proposed_change: Replace the 'serves' predicate with 'applies-to' or 'covers'.

subject: testing.coverageexclusion
text: The references relationships from testing.coverageexclusion to testing.coveragerequirement and to testing.testcoveragetarget are alternative forms of the single excluded item and should be mutually exclusive, with exactly one per exclusion.
proposed_change: Constrain the requirement and target references to be mutually exclusive, requiring exactly one per coverageexclusion.

subject: testing.coverageexclusion
text: The references relationship from testing.coverageexclusion to testing.coveragegap is optional context, because an exclusion can be approved before any gap is recorded.
proposed_change: Mark the coveragegap reference as optional (cardinality 0..1).

subject: testing.coverageexclusion
text: The generic 'references' predicate on testing.coverageexclusion relationships understates the waiver semantics; a dedicated 'excludes' predicate would be clearer.
proposed_change: Replace the 'references' predicate with a dedicated 'excludes' predicate for the exclusion's links to the excluded requirement or target.

subject: testing.coveragegap
text: The relationship testing.coveragegap triggers testing.coveragerequirement overlaps in meaning with testing.coveragegap references testing.coveragerequirement, and inverts the natural dependency because gaps are measured against existing requirements.
proposed_change: Remove the triggers relationship from coveragegap to coveragerequirement and keep only the references relationship.

subject: testing.coveragegap
text: The relationship testing.coveragegap flows-to testing.coverageexclusion describes a lifecycle transition rather than a data or control flow, so the flows-to predicate does not fit.
proposed_change: Replace it with an inverse relationship such as coverageexclusion resolves coveragegap, or use a 'precedes' predicate.

subject: testing.coveragerequirement
text: The relationships accesses and composes from testing.coveragerequirement to testing.inputpartitionselection express the same meaning and are redundant.
proposed_change: Keep one relationship between CoverageRequirement and InputPartitionSelection and remove the other.

subject: testing.coveragerequirement
text: The relationships aggregates and depends-on from testing.coveragerequirement to testing.contextvariation are redundant.
proposed_change: Keep one relationship between CoverageRequirement and ContextVariation and remove the other.

subject: testing.coveragerequirement
text: The relationships composes and depends-on from testing.coveragerequirement to testing.outcomecategory are redundant.
proposed_change: Keep one relationship between CoverageRequirement and OutcomeCategory and remove the other.

subject: testing.coveragerequirement
text: The relationships aggregates and references from testing.coveragerequirement to testing.partitionvalue are redundant.
proposed_change: Keep one relationship between CoverageRequirement and PartitionValue and remove the other.

subject: testing.coveragerequirement
text: The relationships composes and references from testing.coveragerequirement to testing.testcoveragetarget are redundant.
proposed_change: Keep one relationship between CoverageRequirement and TestCoverageTarget and remove the other.

subject: testing.coveragerequirement
text: The composes relationship from testing.coveragerequirement to testing.testcoveragetarget is inverted, because the target owns the requirement (the reverse composition already exists).
proposed_change: Remove the composes relationship from CoverageRequirement to TestCoverageTarget and rely on TestCoverageTarget composes CoverageRequirement.

subject: testing.coveragerequirement
text: The aggregates relationship from testing.coveragerequirement to testing.coverageexclusion is inverted, because the exclusion references the requirement rather than being aggregated by it.
proposed_change: Remove the aggregates relationship and use CoverageExclusion references CoverageRequirement.

subject: testing.coveragerequirement
text: The accesses relationship from testing.coveragerequirement to testing.inputselection crosses into test-case data, which is outside the scope of a coverage requirement.
proposed_change: Remove the accesses relationship from CoverageRequirement to InputSelection.

subject: testing.coveragerequirement
text: OutcomeCategory relationships belong to the TestCoverageTarget rather than to the CoverageRequirement, so the composes and depends-on relationships to outcomecategory are misplaced.
proposed_change: Move the outcome category association to TestCoverageTarget and remove it from CoverageRequirement.

subject: testing.coveragesummary
text: The relationship testing.coveragesummary aggregates testing.testcoveragemodel inverts the containment: the model is reported on by the summary, not part of it.
proposed_change: Remove the aggregates relationship from coveragesummary to testcoveragemodel.

subject: testing.environmentfactor
text: The relationship testing.environmentfactor composes testing.inputspacepartition contradicts the EnvironmentFactor definition, since a factor describes the environment, not input to the system under test.
proposed_change: Remove the composes relationship from environmentfactor to inputspacepartition.

subject: testing.environmentfactor
text: The relationship testing.environmentfactor references testing.partitionvalue is suspect because PartitionValue models input equivalence classes, not environment properties.
proposed_change: Remove the references relationship from environmentfactor to partitionvalue.

subject: testing.environmentfactor
text: The relationship testing.environmentfactor composes testing.contextvariation should likely be aggregates, because factors are optionally bound to variations and can be shared among them.
proposed_change: Change the predicate from composes to aggregates.

subject: testing.environmentfactor
text: The relationship testing.environmentfactor flows-to testing.coveragesummary is odd, since coverage summaries total targets, requirements and sketches, not environment factors.
proposed_change: Remove the flows-to relationship from environmentfactor to coveragesummary.

subject: testing.environmentfactor
text: The relationship testing.environmentfactor serves testing.testcoveragemodel likely should be expressed as composed-by or aggregated-by, reversing its direction or predicate.
proposed_change: Replace serves with a composed-by or aggregated-by relationship between testcoveragemodel and environmentfactor.

subject: testing.inputpartitionselection
text: The aggregates relationship from testing.inputpartitionselection to testing.contextvariation looks misplaced, because a selection names one partition and its values and contexts belong to the CoverageRequirement, not the selection.
proposed_change: Remove the aggregates relationship from InputPartitionSelection to ContextVariation and attach contexts to CoverageRequirement instead.

subject: testing.inputpartitionselection
text: The relationship from testing.inputpartitionselection to testing.partitionvalue should use 'references' rather than 'aggregates', since values are owned by the InputSpacePartition and an exclude-form selection only points at them.
proposed_change: Change the predicate of the InputPartitionSelection to PartitionValue relationship from aggregates to references.

subject: testing.inputselection
text: The relationship testing.inputselection references testing.testcoveragetarget is redundant because the owning TestCaseSketch already attaches to exactly one target and PartitionValue reaches the target via InputSpacePartition, so the link is derivable and risks inconsistency.
proposed_change: Remove the references relationship from testing.inputselection to testing.testcoveragetarget.

subject: testing.inputselection
text: The CoverageRequirement reference should sit on TestCaseSketch rather than InputSelection, because requirements apply to combinations of selections, not to single bindings.
proposed_change: Remove the references relationship from testing.inputselection to testing.coveragerequirement and add an equivalent relationship from testing.testcasesketch to testing.coveragerequirement.

subject: testing.inputspacepartition
text: The four references relationships from testing.inputspacepartition to data-store.collection, data-model.jsonschema, api.parameter and data-model.schemaproperty are alternative anchors for the single field, so a partition should reference exactly one of them, which the catalog does not express.
proposed_change: Document or enforce that a partition references exactly one of collection, jsonschema, parameter or schemaproperty.

subject: testing.inputspacepartition
text: The references relationship from testing.inputspacepartition to data-model.jsonschema targets a whole schema document, which is coarser than a field-level reference and overlaps with the reference to data-model.schemaproperty.
proposed_change: Remove the references relationship to data-model.jsonschema in favour of the schemaproperty reference.

subject: testing.inputspacepartition
text: The serves relationship from testing.inputspacepartition to testing.testcoveragetarget would read more naturally as composed-of or aggregated-by.
proposed_change: Replace the serves predicate with composes or aggregates (composed-of or aggregated-by).

subject: testing.outcomecategory
text: The relationship testing.outcomecategory aggregates testing.testcasesketch overlaps with the sketch's own depends-on reference to the outcome category, and is likely redundant with the inverse testcasesketch-to-outcomecategory link.
proposed_change: Remove one of the two relationships, likely the outcomecategory aggregates testcasesketch relationship, keeping the sketch-to-outcome link.

subject: testing.outcomecategory
text: The relationship testing.outcomecategory flows-to testing.coveragesummary is weak because the coverage summary totals targets, requirements and sketches, not outcome categories.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: testing.outcomecategory
text: The relationship testing.outcomecategory constrained-by testing.environmentfactor is plausible but loose, since outcomes are classified per target rather than per environment factor.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: testing.outcomecategory
text: The relationship testing.outcomecategory references testing.targetinputfield is plausible but loose, since outcomes are classified per target rather than per input field.
proposed_change: none stated

subject: testing.partitiondependency
text: The relationship testing.partitiondependency --constrained-by--> testing.inputpartitionselection looks inverted, because a dependency restricts which combinations a selection yields, so 'constrains' fits better.
proposed_change: Replace 'constrained-by' with 'constrains' for the relationship from partitiondependency to inputpartitionselection.

subject: testing.partitiondependency
text: The 'triggers' relationship from testing.partitiondependency to testing.coveragerequirement is semantically weak, and 'constrains' would be more accurate.
proposed_change: Replace 'triggers' with 'constrains' for the relationship from partitiondependency to coveragerequirement.

subject: testing.partitiondependency
text: The 'triggers' relationship from testing.partitiondependency to testing.partitionvalue conflates the trigger value that activates the dependency with the affected values.
proposed_change: Rework the 'triggers' relationship toward partitionvalue so it no longer conflates the trigger value with the affected values.

subject: testing.partitiondependency
text: testing.partitiondependency lacks a 'triggered-by' relationship to testing.partitionvalue identifying the trigger value that activates the dependency.
proposed_change: Add a 'triggered-by' relationship from testing.partitiondependency to testing.partitionvalue for the trigger value.

subject: testing.partitionvalue
text: The relationship testing.partitionvalue --[references]--> testing.coverageexclusion is questionable because exclusions apply to coverage targets or requirements, not to partition values.
proposed_change: Remove the references relationship from PartitionValue to CoverageExclusion.

subject: testing.partitionvalue
text: The relationship testing.partitionvalue --[triggers]--> testing.coveragegap is loose because gaps are defined against requirements or targets and are produced by an analysis process, not by the partition value itself.
proposed_change: Remove or replace the triggers relationship from PartitionValue to CoverageGap with one tied to requirements or targets.

subject: testing.partitionvalue
text: The relationship testing.partitionvalue --[depends-on]--> testing.environmentfactor mixes input-space and environment concerns that the definitions keep separate.
proposed_change: Remove the depends-on relationship from PartitionValue to EnvironmentFactor.

subject: testing.targetcoveragesummary
text: The 'validates' relationship from testing.targetcoveragesummary to testing.coveragerequirement overstates the summary's role, since it only reports measured status and verifies nothing; 'measures' or 'tracks' would fit better.
proposed_change: Change the predicate from 'validates' to 'measures' or 'tracks'.

subject: testing.targetcoveragesummary
text: The 'validates' relationship from testing.targetcoveragesummary to testing.testcoveragetarget overstates the summary's role, since it only reports measured status and verifies nothing; 'measures' or 'tracks' would fit better.
proposed_change: Change the predicate from 'validates' to 'measures' or 'tracks'.

subject: testing.targetcoveragesummary
text: The validates edge from testing.targetcoveragesummary to testing.testcoveragetarget is redundant with the edge to testing.coveragerequirement, because requirements attach to the target.
proposed_change: Remove the target edge and keep the requirement edge.

subject: testing.targetcoveragesummary
text: The 'aggregates' relationship from testing.targetcoveragesummary to testing.testcasesketch is closer to counting than aggregation, so 'references' or 'measures' would fit better.
proposed_change: Change the predicate from 'aggregates' to 'references' or 'measures'.

subject: testing.targetinputfield
text: The maps-to relationship from testing.targetinputfield to ux.actioncomponent is wrong because input fields correspond to UI input components rather than action controls, and maps-to is a data schema predicate.
proposed_change: Remove or retarget the maps-to relationship to a UI input component type and use a predicate that fits the semantics.

subject: testing.targetinputfield
text: The aggregates relationship from testing.targetinputfield to testing.partitionvalue is redundant because the references relationship to testing.inputspacepartition already reaches partition values.
proposed_change: Remove the aggregates relationship to testing.partitionvalue.

subject: testing.targetinputfield
text: The references relationship from testing.targetinputfield to testing.testcoveragetarget understates what is really composition, duplicating the composes relationship from testcoveragetarget.
proposed_change: Replace the references relationship with composition, or drop it in favor of the existing composes relationship.

subject: testing.testcasesketch
text: The relationships tests, validates and references from testcasesketch to CoverageRequirement overlap in meaning; only references and validates should be kept.
proposed_change: Remove the tests relationship to CoverageRequirement and keep references and validates.

subject: testing.testcasesketch
text: The references and validates relationships from testcasesketch to TestCoverageTarget overlap in meaning.
proposed_change: Collapse the two into a single relationship (one of references or validates).

subject: testing.testcasesketch
text: The accesses relationship from testcasesketch to InputSelection duplicates the composes relationship to InputSelection.
proposed_change: Remove the accesses relationship to InputSelection and keep composes.

subject: testing.testcasesketch
text: The accesses relationship from testcasesketch to InputPartitionSelection is a design-time lookup and is better expressed as references.
proposed_change: Replace accesses with references for InputPartitionSelection.

subject: testing.testcasesketch
text: The fulfills-requirements relationship from testcasesketch to motivation.requirement mislabels verification as realization; validates fits better.
proposed_change: Replace fulfills-requirements with validates.

subject: testing.testcasesketch
text: The references relationship to apm.logconfiguration and the supports-goals relationship to motivation.goal are weak links of little value.
proposed_change: Remove the references LogConfiguration and supports-goals relationships.

subject: testing.testcoveragemodel
